            (xi)     A sum of Rs.30.11 crore has been left unutilized by Tuticorin Port due to change in design of berth No. 9,
 delay in replacement of equipments, delay in tenders which were invited for formation of new roads etc.
            (xii)    In Cochin Port an amount of Rs.9.25 crore was unutilized due to re-tendering for installation of 110 KV
 sub-station at Mattancherry halt. Rs.4.00 crore was unutilized for the Thevara Foreshore Reclamation
 Scheme as the tenders had to be cancelled due to opposition by local residents.
            (xiii)   There has been shortfall of Rs.l90 crore in utilization of Plan allocation of Dredging Corporation of India.
 Of this shortfall of Rs.35 crore was’because of delay in placement of order for replacement of Dredger Dr.
 VII as a result of which only first stage payment of Rs.25 crore could be made during the year as against
 the planned two stage payment totaling Rs.60 crore. Rs.80 crore allocated for procurement of new TSHD
 could not be utilized because the tender for the same had to be discharged. Rs.34 crore allocated for Dumb
 Backhoe Dredger could not be utilized since the specifications for the same had to be changed so as to be
 compatible with the need for dredging of hard material and rock. Floating of tenders had to be deferred to
 2006-07 pending finalization of the technical specifications. Rs.29 crore allocated for Self propelled
 Barges (2 Nos.) could not be utilized due to change in technical specifications and consequent deferment
 of the scheme for 2006-07.
11.   In some of the cases, the reasons for non-utilization of allocation were beyond the control of Port Management.
 The Port Management have been advised to ensure a more realistic budget and strict implementation and monitoring.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
12.   The Committee notes that there has been a time lag between formulation process for different schemes
 under annual plan and implementation period, due to which, there was a mismatch between the allocation and
 the actual expenditure. The Committee further notes that in order to fill the gap, the Port Trusts have been
 advised to be realistic in approach while proposing the annual plan outlay and only token provision are to be
 kept for projects for which administrative approval is yet to be accorded by the Competent Authority. The
 Department of Shipping has also put into place a monitoring mechanism for regular review of plan expenditure
 on monthly and quarterly basis. The Committee however, does not agree with the contention of the Department
 of Shipping that there is no major shortfall in the utilization of Gross Budgetary Support (BE) during 2005-06,
 and the reasons put forth by the Department are not such which can not be anticipated in advance. The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to ensure a more realistic budget and strict
 implementation and monitoring so as to speed up the pace of expenditure during the next fiscal year.
CAPACITY ENHANCEMENT IN MAJOR PORTS
(Recommendation at Para 19)
13.   The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping is implementing the schemes for enhancing the
 capacity and productivity of all major ports and to encourage the private sector participation for the
 development of ports infrastructure and accordingly, comprehensive policy guidelines have been issued. The
 Committee also notes that the Government has allowed cent percent FDI for construction and maintenance of
 ports in order to mobilize substantial resources as well as to improve efficiency, productivity and quality of
 services of Ports. The Committee, however, observed that as against the capacity of 408.60 million TPA, the
 major ports handled a total traffic of 310.80 mt. upto December, 2005. This way, the aggregate capacity of major
 ports exceeds the traffic target marginally. Therefore, there is need to increase capacity of ports on urgent basis.
 The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to take action for development of
 infrastructure in major ports so as to face global competition of sea-borne trade and enhance private sector
 investment including FDI in the sector by addressing the procedural rigidity expediting well integrated and
 coordinated policy framework and approach.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
14.   The aggregate cargo handling capacity of the 12 major ports as on 31.3.2006 is 456.20 MT which takes into
 account the addition of berths and improvement in productivity. In 2005-06, the major ports handled traffic of 423.42
 MT. The traffic target in 2006-07 is 465.70 MT. In 2006-07, it is anticipated that three new berths would be
 commissioned which would add a capacity of 26.40 MT thereby taking the capacity of 482.60 MT at the end of 10th
 Plan against the 10th Plan target of 470 MT. Under the National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP)
 formulated by the Department of Shipping, it is planned to augment the aggregate capacity of the major ports to 800.41
 MTPA by 2011-2012. Under the programme , a total 276 projects covering the entire gamut of activities in the major
 ports including berths development, deepening of channels, equipment upgradation, rail/road connectivity and other
 associated activities have been identified which are to be implemented in two phases through Public Private
 Participation (PPP). Out of the total estimated investment of Rs.55,803.73 crore under the scheme, an amount of
 34,505.34 crore is envisaged through private investment including foreign direct investment.

FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
15.   The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping has been taking measures for enhancing capacity of
 major ports due to which the aggregate cargo handling capacity at major ports as on March 31, 2006 was 456.20
 Mt. and the major ports handled traffic of 423.42 Mt. as against traffic target of 465.70 Mt. The Committee also
 notes that the Department of Shipping has been planning to augment the aggregate capacity of the major ports
 to 800.41MTPA by  2011-12 under the National Maritime Development Programme  with the total estimated
 investment of Rs.55, 830.73 crore  under the scheme out of which Rs.34,505.34 crore has been envisaged through
 private sector investment including FDI. The Committee recommends the Department to identify the host of
 activities in the major ports for capacity enhancement and remove the procedural hurdles, if any, by adhering to
 a coordinated policy framework and approach in their future plan.
PORT LABOUR REFORMS
(Recommendation at Para 21)
16.   The Committee notes that in the changed fiscal regime the Government is committed for labour reforms and
 desires to allow private sector investment for creation and augmentation of capacity building in the port
 infrastructure. The Committee also notes with concern that enhancement of private sector investment for
 development of port infrastructure may deter the interest of employees unions/federations. Therefore, the
 Committee feels that the port labour reforms are necessary before exposing the labour sector to open market
 mechanism. In view of this, the Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to de-regulate and
 decentralize the commercial environment for collective bargaining to improve the productivity levels at ports
 while taking adequate care of labour interests.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
17.   The existing guidelines on private sector participation in port projects provide that while handing over the existing
 facilities to the private operator, the labour, which has necessarily to be taken over by the private operator, should be
 included in the tender document. This takes care of the concern expressed by the Committee. However, in respect of
 BOT projects, which are developed by private operator, there obviously cannot be any pre­ condition like that because
 the project is being developed by the operator in green field site. The Government is committed to safeguard the
 interests of the labour in Port sector and the following institutional arrangements are in operation in major ports for
 addressing theconcerns of labour:—
            (i)      Port labour reforms are a continuing process and various demands of the Major Federations of Port and
 dock Workers are discussed and considered from time to time and all possible measures are taken to meet
 their demands.
            (ii)      The wages structure of Portand Dock employees (Class III and IV) was revised after every 5 years
 through a Bi-partite Wage Negotiations Committee (BWNC). The Committee consists of representatives
 of Port Management and Federations of Workers. From 1.1.1997, the duration of wage structure is
 extended to 10 years, at par with Central Government employees. Various demands/grievances of workers
 relating to wage structure are considered by the BWNC.
            (iii)      For improving the productivity levels, it is very essential to rationalize the manning scales. This matter
 had been referred by this Ministry to M/O Labour for adjudication by National Tribunal. The award of the
 National Tribunal has now been received from M/O Labour and further action for rationalizing manning
 scales and datums for the purpose of improving productivity will be taken in the light of the award of the
 National Tribunal in consultation with Major Port Trusts.
            (iv)     On the Boards of each Major Port Trust two seats have been earmarked for trustees representing labour
 and in this way the interests of labour are properly safeguarded at Board level. Similarly, the
 representatives of labour are also appointed on the existing Dock Labour Boards.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
18.   The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping has been taking adequate care to safeguard the
 interest of the labour engaged in Port Sector by making institutional arrangements in major ports for
 addressing the concerns of the port labour. The Committee further notes that the guidelines on private sector
 participation in port projects provides that while handing over the existing facilities to the private operator, the
 labour, which has necessarily to be taken over by the private operator, should be included in the tender
 document. However, in respect of BOT projects, which are developed by private operator, there obviously
 cannot be any pre-condition like that because the project is being developed by the operator in green field site.
 The Committee while agreeing to the replies of the Department of Shipping, recommends that Government
 should explore the possibility of having some effective mechanism in place so as to ensure that there is no
 exploitation of labour engaged in the BOT projects.

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/114.htm[28-08-2018 13:24:01]
PORT CONNECTIVITY
(Recommendation at Para 23)
19.   The Committee observes that the lack of proper port connectivity has hampered the development of ports.
 The Committee also notes that projects involving 117.73 km. for improving road accessibility to Ports have been
 completed and projects involving 313.85 kms. of road length are under implementation. The Committee is of the
 view that development of other modes of transport viz. railways, highways and inland water transport is also
 essential for improving the accessibility to ports and to keep pace with the growing requirements of overseas
 trade. The Committee feels that the availability of such modal mix will result in considerable saving in cost and
 time for cargo containers assessing these ports. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of
 Shipping to take steps for better road and rail connectivity infrastructure in all the major ports for the growth
 of the container cargo. The cost of connectivity could be
 shared in public sector by the strategic partners or alternatively, the private public partnership (PPP) or joint
 venture partnership (JVP) could also be explored.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
20.   Government recognizes the importance of providing adequate connectivity to the Ports and augmentation of Port
 connectivity infrastructure is undertaken on a continuous basis depending upon traffic requirements. The Committee on
 Infrastructure (CoI) held by Hon’ble Prime Minister, had set up a Committee of Secretaries (CoS) to review the rail-
road connectivity in Major Ports. The CoS submitted its report in February 2006 to CoI which accepted the
 recommendations made by CoS. Briefly, major recommendations made by CoS are:—
            (i)      Each Major Port should preferably have minimum four lane road and double line rail connectivity. The
 connectivity should be established in fixed time-frame.
            (ii)      All projects with less than the minimum prescribed IRR, would be considered on case to case basis.
            (iii)      COS recommended that budgetary assistance under the Viability Gap Funding Scheme could be
 considered on case to case basis.
            (iv)     Road connectivity projects may be broadly divided into two categories:-
                            (a)    Port Connectivity - projects where the length of the road is not very long (less than 50 Km.); and
                            (b)   Hinterland Connectivity - projects where connectivity to source of cargo such as iron ore
 mines/coal mines is to be provided.
            (v)     Schemes for undertaking Port Connectivity would be undertaken by NHAI on BOT basis. The National
 Highways for Port connectivity may be categorized as National Highways (Port Connectivity).
            (vi)     State Highways with a traffic intensity of 10,000 PCUs or more should be declared as National Highways
 as per extant procedure.
            (vii)    All National Highways (Port Connectivity) where the traffic count reaches 12,000 PCUs should be taken
 up for four laning on priority.
            (viii)    All NH (PC) projects would be taken up by NHAI as per normal parameters. However, separate tolling
 policy for NH(PC) could be proposed jointly by the NHAI and the Shipping Department where necessary.
            (ix)     All proposals for roads falling in the category of hinterland connectivity would be taken up by NHAI on
 BOT basis, as far as possible.
            (x)     CoS recommended completion of the nine ongoing projects for augmentation of road connectivity as per
 schedule and recommended four projects for sanction.
            (xi)     CoS recommended timely completion of eight sanctioned/ongoing projects and recommended five
 projects for which the Railways have carried out or are currently carrying out surveys with a view to
 determining the viability of these projects. Action is being taken for implementation of the
 recommendations which would improve the existing connectivity of all major ports.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
21.   The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping has taken steps for providing adequate connectivity
 to the port and augmentation of port connectivity infrastructure on continuous basis depending upon the traffic
 requirement The Committee further notes that the Committee of Secretaries (CoS) has been set up to review the
 rail-road connectivity in major ports and has submitted its report to the Government. The Committee
 recommends that the Department of Shipping should take action for implementation of the recommendations of

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/114.htm[28-08-2018 13:24:01]
 Committee of Secretaries, which would definitely improve the existing rail-road connectivity of all major ports.
CONTAINERIZATION IN MAJOR PORTS
(Recommendation at Para 27)
22.   The Committee observes that the international trade is witnessing an increasing trend towards
 containerization. However, the Committee is constrained to note that the major ports did not-significantly
 contribute to export-import trade and about 70 percent of containers are trans-shipped at neighborhood
 international Ports such as, Colombo, Dubai and Singapore Ports, making thereby India’s export costlier and
 imports less competitive. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Government should establish hub ports in
 the country preferably, in East and West Coast for trans-shipment of containerized cargo for the growth of sea-
borne overseas trade and economic development.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
23.   Dedicated capacities for handling containerized cargo is available in seven major ports, namely, Kolkata Port (both
 at Kolkata Dock Systems and Haldia Dock Complex), Visakhapatnam Port, Chennai Port, Tuticorin Port, Cochin Port,
 Mumbai Port and Jawaharlal Nehru Port. The total capacity available at these seven ports is 5.18 million Twenty Feet
 Equivalent Units (TEUs).
24.   A hub port is required to fulfil certain requirements such as required volume of traffic, proximity to international
 routes and markets, long waterfront, deep draught, good road/rail connectivity, large backup area and supporting
 hinterland. In India, Jawaharlal Nehru Port on the west coast with the northern and north-western regions of India and
 Chennai Port on the east coast with the southern and south-east regions of India as their main hinterland are operating
 as regional hub ports. About 92 per cent of container cargo at Jawaharlal  Nehru Port and about 44 per cent of container
 cargo at Chennai Port during 2005-06 were ‘direct to destination’ cargoes without involving transhipment in any port
 abroad. About 65 per cent of container cargo at Tuticorin Port was also direct to destination. Overall, about 66 per cent
 of container cargo handled in the major ports during 2005-06 were direct to destination.
25.   Chennai  Port has adequate draft to handle majority of modern large size container vessels visiting India. One
 container terminal at Chennai Port with a capacity for handling one million Twenty Feet Equivalent Units (TEUs) per
 annum is already operational. Selection of a bidder for development, operation and management of a second container
 terminal at the port on Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT) basis is under finalization. After completion of the second
 container terminal, Chennai Port will have capacity for handling 1.8 million TEUs per annum. Projects for improving
 connectivity from the port to its hinterland have also been planned.
26.   At Jawaharlal Nehru Port, Two container terminals and one shallow water berth with a capacity for handling 2.55
 million TEUs per annum are already operational in the port. The third container terminal at the port is currently under
 construction and is expected to be fully operational in October, 2006. Additional container handling capacity on
 account of the third container terminal in the port will be 1.3 million TEUs. Thus, on operationalisation  of the third

 cannot be any pre-condition like that because the project is being developed by the operator in green field site.

 should explore the possibility of having some effective mechanism in place so as to ensure that there is no
 exploitation of labour engaged in the BOT projects.                                                                                                     
 (Para 18)
PORT CONNECTIVITY
        The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping has taken steps for providing adequate connectivity
 to the port and augmentation of port connectivity infrastructure on continuous basis depending upon the traffic
 requirement The Committee further notes that the Committee of Secretaries (COS) has been set up to review
 the rail-road connectivity in major ports and has submitted its report to the Government. The Committee
 recommends that the Department of Shipping should take action for implementation of the recommendations of
 Committee of Secretaries, which would definitely improve the existing rail-road connectivity of all major
 ports.        (Para 21)
CONTAINERIZATION IN MAJOR PORTS
        The Committee notes that Jawaharlal Nehru Port on the west coast with the northern and north-western
 regions of the country and Chennai Port on the east coast with the southern and south-east regions of the
 country as their main hinterland are operating as regional hub ports. The forthcoming Valarpadam Port must
 be developed as a regional hub port as well. The Committee also notes that during 2005-06, about 66 per cent of
 container cargo handled in the major ports including Jawaharlal Nehru Port, Chennai Port and Tuticorin Port
 were direct to destination cargoes without involving transshipment in any port abroad. The Committee

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/114.htm[28-08-2018 13:24:01]
 appreciates the Department of Shipping for taking measures for augmenting the capacities for handling
 containers in the major ports for the growth of sea-borne overseas trade. The Committee expects that
 Development of regional hub ports and the International Container Transshipment Terminals and measures
 taken by the Government to develop container handling facilities in other major ports coupled with development
 of container handling facilities at some non-major ports will result in decline of transshipment of Indian cargo at
 ports outside India and bring economic development.                                                               (Para 30)
SETHUSAMUDRAM SHIP CHANNEL PROJECT
        The Committee notes that while formulating the Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project adequate care has
 been taken by the Department of Shipping to ensure that adverse impact on environment is minimal. An
 elaborate Environment Management Plan has been drawn up to safeguard the Bio-diversity of the region during
 project implementation and operation period. The Committee also notes that a monitoring committee has been
 set up to assess the impact of dredging work on environment including assessment of marine water quality,
 sediment quality, ambient air quality and the noise level and other protests that have arisen with regard to the
 project. The Committee recommends that the measures being observed by the Department of Shipping should
 adequately address the environment concerns as a part of the implementation of the Project and Committee
 should be apprised of net result achieved therefrom.                                                                (Para 35)
NATIONAL MARITIME DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME
        The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping is in agreement with the need for implementation of
 the National Maritime Development Programme  activities besides developing and adding to the infrastructure
 for capacity building both in terms of human resources, technology up-gradation as well as research and
 development. The Committee also notes that there already exist institutional arrangements within the
 Department of Shipping for implementation of different projects identified under National Maritime
 Programme and desires not to pursue the recommendation further.                                                             (Para 39)
EXTENDING TONNAGE TAX BENEFIT TO INLAND VESSELS AND COASTAL VESSELS
        The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping is taking up the matter with the Ministry of Finance
 for extending tonnage tax benefits to the vessels registered under Inland Vessels Act and Coasting Vessel Act.
 The Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for delay in extending the benefits of tonnage tax to the
 vessels registered under Inland Vessels Act and Coasting Vessel Act. The Committee feels that the Government
 would not be able to develop the inland water transport and coastal vessel transport in the country, unless the
 benefit of tonnage tax and Section 33 AC of Income Tax Act were not granted to these vessels. In this regard, the
 Committee reiterates its earlier recommendations contained in 105th Report of the Committee, which is
 reproduced below:
“The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to vigorously pursue the matter
 with the Ministry of Finance for inclusion of the Vessels registered under Inland Vesselsand Coastal
 Vessels Acts under the tonnage tax regime so as to unfold the infrastructure potential of IWT sector
 with the growth of the Indian economy.”
                                                                                                                                        (Para 42)
CALCUTTA DOCK LABOUR BOARD
        The Committee is constrained to note that the Government is dilly-dallying the matter which has aggravated
 the problem of employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board in getting the pension and pensionary benefits. The
 Committee feels that every delay in release of grant to Calcutta Dock Labour Board for payment of unpaid
 arrears and meeting the future superannuation liabilities of employees will burden the Government heavily, if
 not tackled now. The Committee is of the strong view that injustice is being meted to the employees of Calcutta
 Dock Labour Board in the matter of payment of the pension and pensionary dues on time after retirement and
 recommends that the Government should come out with one time concrete proposal which would adequately
 address the total revenue requirement of employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board instead of doing it in a
 piecemeal manner.                                                                                                                       (Para 45)
MISAPPROPRIATION OF SEAMEN’S PROVIDENT FUND
        The Committee notes with dismay that the Government had not yet taken a final decision in the matter of
 recouping the shortage of Rs.92.78 crore  in Seamen’s Provident Fund so far. The Committee urges upon the
 Government that the hard earned money of Seamen’s which was being pilferaged in the scam because of faulty
 Government policy should be recouped in the fund by releasing one time grant of Rs.92.78 crore in the Seamen’s
 Provident Fund so that the hardships being faced by the Seamen’s could be eased to some extent.   
                                                                                                                                                       (Para 48)

        The Committee notes that the draft Indian Maritime University Bill has been prepared and is being
 examined in the Department of Shipping. The Committee further notes that the IMU Bill alongwith the
 recommendations of the Expenditure Finance Committee will be placed before the Cabinet shortly for
 consideration. The Committee therefore, urges upon the Government to take an early decision on the formation
 of the Indian Maritime University under the Central Act in consultation with all stakeholders.

CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
        The Committee does not see any merit in the decision of the Government for disinvestment of Central
 Inland Water Transport Corporation. The Committee is of the view that Inland Water Transport Sector cannot
 survive without Government investment in the infrastructure and CIWTC has to play the role of catalyst for
 that sector. The Committee recommends the Government to reconsider the decision for disinvestment of the
 Central Inland Water Transport Corporation for want of exploiting opportunity in the IWT Sector in the
 Country. The Committee further recommends that CIWTC be either merged with Kolkata Port Trust or be
 taken over by IWTA in order to further augment the infrastructure in the eastern and north eastern regions.
 (Para 55)
INLAND WATER TRANSPORT
        The Committee notes that Government have decided to develop the existing three National Waterways fully
 functional by March 2008 with an estimated investment of about Rs.630 crore . The Committee also notes that
 the Department of Shipping has adopted several measures for encouraging private investment and developing
 institutional framework for IWT Sector in the country and Development of IWT has already been included
 under the National Maritime Development Programme. The Committee expects that after the three National
 waterways are made fully functional, commercial viability of IWT operations on these waterways will improve
 and then private sector will come forward to invest in ownership and operation of inland vessels and later on in
 development of infrastructure as well for the overall development and viability of this sector.

This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the
 observations/ recommendations as contained in its One-Hundred and Sixth Report on Demands for Grants (2006-07) of
 Ministry of Civil Aviation, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 27th February, 2006.
 
 2.         Action Taken Replies have been received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 10 th November, 2006 in
 respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report, which have been categorised as follows: -
 
(i)         Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry:
Para Nos. 15, 25, 32, 34, 68, 78, 92, 93, 99, 102, 118, 121, 133 &
139                                                                                                            Total- 14
(ii)        Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Ministry’s
 replies:
Para No.                                                                                                          Nil.
(iii)       Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have not been accepted by the
 Committee:
Para Nos. 19,  23, 27, 64, 73,  108, 123, 129, 141                                          Total- 9
(iv)       Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the    Ministry are still awaited:
Para No. 20, 104, 135                                                                                                 3
 
3.         The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of Action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry.  The recommendations of the Committee contained in the One-Hundred
 and Sixth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry, and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each
 item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
ASSESSMENT OF ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06 AND ALLOCATION FOR    2006-07
(Recommendation at Para 15)
 
5.         The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry has taken due cognizance of its earlier recommendations
 pertaining to utilisation of budget allocations and has made efforts to improve the earlier situation of consistent
 underutilization of funds.  The Committee notes that barring the low proportion of expenditure of Pawan Hans
 Helicopters Limited, the anticipated expenditure in respect of other organisations is satisfactory vis-a-vis the approved
 allocations.  The Committee, however expresses its concern that the Gross Budgetary Support has been reduced from
 Rs.370.85 crore in 2005-06 to Rs.130.00 crore in 2006-07.  The Committee expects that the targets set for internal and
 extra budgetary resources as well as external commercial borrowings from foreign banks/financial institutions for
 bridging the gap in budgetary support will materialize.  The Committee recommends that  the Ministry should take
 adequate steps during 2006-07 also to ensure optimum utilisation of the enhanced allocations made to various
 organisations.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
6.         The reduction in Plan Outlay during 2006-07 was primarily due to the fact that no provision had been made for
 payment of budgetary support to Indian Airlines during 2006-07.  A provision of Rs.325 crores had been made during
 2005-06 for payment of budgetary support to Indian Airlines in connection with their aircraft acquisition project which
 was released during the year.  The balance expenditure on aircraft acquisition project was to be met by Indian Airlines
 out of their internal and extra budgetary resources including external commercial borrowings.  The observations of the

 Committee with regard to optimum utilization plan allocations for 2006-07 have been noted for compliance.
 
 
AIR INDIA LIMITED
(Recommendation at Para 19)
 
7.         The Committee notes that the outlay for non-aircraft projects is an important component of the budget provision
 for Air India Limited as the programmes/projects undertaken there under viz. purchase of Ground Handling
 Equipments, Engineering Workshop Equipments, Security Equipments, Aircraft Refurbishment Programme etc. are
 aimed at enhancing the operational efficiency.   The Committee expects that the allocated funds would be fully utilised
 during 2006-07 and recommends that the Ministry should take suitable steps to ensure that the operational efficiency of
 Air India Limited is not compromised for want of funds.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
8.         The recommendations of the Committee has been noted for compliance.  It would be ensured that operational
 efficiency of Air India Limited is not compromised for want of funds.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
9.         The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and desires to know actual details
 of the programmes/projects undertaken viz. purchase of Ground Handling Equipments, Engineering Workshop
 Equipments, Security Equipments, Aircraft Refurbishment Programme etc. and how much amount was spent on these
 projects out of the total outlay.  The Committee also desires the Ministry to furnish detail about the steps taken during
 the year to improve the operational efficiency of Air India Limited.
 
 
 
(Recommendation at 
Para 20)
 
10.       The Committee notes that Air India has been reporting net profits consistently since 2001-02 and expects that
 this healthy situation will continue. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should endeavour to focus on all the
 individual parameters that enhance the overall operational performance with the available aircraft capacity till new and
 modern aircraft join its fleet.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
11.       The observations of the Committee have been noted.   Every endeavour is being made to enhance the operational
 performance of Air India to meet the ever increasing challenges in the aviation market.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
12.       The Committee desires that the recommendation should be taken seriously and reiterates its recommendation
 that the Ministry should endeavor to focus on all the individual parameters that enhance the overall operational
 performance with the available aircraft capacity till new and modern aircraft join its fleet.
 
(Recommendation at Para 23)
 
13.       The level of Passenger Load Factor has a direct impact on the profit/loss balance sheet. The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that Air India should adopt aggressive marketing strategies to improve its Passenger Load
 Factor to the desired level.  The Committee also recommends that the bilateral air services agreements should be
 leveraged to diversify the international air services and to avail the entitlements of new traffic rights to the full extent.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT

14.       Air India has been following aggressive marketing practices to improve its Passenger Load Factors, and
 consequently its revenue and profitability.  Some of measures undertaken by Air India are :
 
a)          Launching of a low cost carrier, Air India Express;
 
b)          Leasing of 28 aircraft (including 7 for Air India Express) to increase its market share and reach;
 
c)
          Acquisition of 68 new aircraft (including 18 for Air India Express) to improve the product and cut
 maintenance, fuel and other costs;
 
 
d)
          Introduction of non-stop flights, standardized timings, better connectivity from interior points in India;
 
e)
          Commenced direct marketing practices to reach customers personally;
 
f)
            Improvement in overall product with installation of flat beds in First Class and Soubrettes in Executive Class
 of all B747-400 aircraft and introduction of schemes like Premium Traveler Programme and Companion Free
 Scheme to improve utilization of First and Executive Class;
 
g)
          Introduction of customer friendly facilities like e-ticketing, advance check-in,   city check-in at Mumbai
 Airport, domestic and international call centers, etc;
 
h)
          Frequent Flyer Programme, Maharaja Club and Leading Edge Club to give high yield passengers recognition
 and value added benefits to retain their loyalty;.
 
15.       With the acquisition of new aircraft, Air India will have additional flights on routes which are commercially and
 economically viable, thus improving utilization of traffic rights.
 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
16.       The Committee notes that the Air India has taken some measure to improve its passenger load factors.  However,
 the Committee takes exception to the fact that Ministry remains silent on its recommendation that the "bilateral air
 services agreements should be leveraged to diversify the international air services and to avail the entitlement of new
 traffic rights to the full extent."  The Committee desires to have action by the Ministry in the matter.
 
(Recommendation at 
Para 25)
 
17.       The Committee notes that important announcements have been made in the Annual Supplement, 2006 under the
 Foreign Trade Policy 2004-09, which inter-alia, will enable the country to offer competitive fuel prices and attract mid
 route stops for international flights and they are likely to play a catalytic role in the growth of civil aviation sector. The
 Committee recommends that the Ministry should pursue the matter regarding the issuance of notifications specifying
 the scope and extent of concessions/exemptions with the Commerce Ministry/Finance Ministry for deriving the
 anticipated benefits from the announcements made in the Annual Supplement, 2006 under the Foreign Trade Policy
 2004-09.   The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should initiate suitable steps in advance to facilitate
 the National Carriers to avail the full benefits of the announcements.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
18.       Necessary provisions for allowing duty neutralization benefits to supply of stores on board foreign going
 aircraft, through Advance Authorisation Scheme, have been made in para 4.1.3 of the Foreign Trade Policy (2004-09). 
 Department of Revenue have also issued necessary instructions for implementation of this facility by the Customs
 authorities.  Since the entire scheme is intended to reduce the cost of stores for foreign going aircraft by neutralizing the

115 th Report of Committe on Industry

 duty incidence on inputs required for manufacture of these goods, Air India, Indian Airlines and other airlines can
 obtain the benefits of this scheme through a proportionate cost reduction by the manufacturers of stores.  Air India and
 Indian Airlines are being advised to suitably negotiate with their suppliers.
 
(Recommendation at Para 27)
 
19.       The Committee notes that Air India had approached only M/s. Jet Airways in July, 2005 to negotiate the wet-
lease of one A340-330E aircraft.  The Committee is of the opinion that Air India could have approached other Airlines
 organisations.  The procedure followed by Air India was against the practice of open competitive tendering process and
 therefore lacks transparency.  The Committee feels that the impending shortage could have been anticipated early had
 there been a constant assessment of the available aircraft capacity. The Committee further recommends that adequate
 contingency plans should be prepared including standing arrangements for lease of aircraft during exigencies by
 following the proper tendering process.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
20.       The lease of aircraft by Air India from Jet Airways was a very short term arrangement.   However, observations
 of the Committee in this regard have been noted by Air India for future guidance. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
21.       The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and desires to know whether
 there are any policy/guidelines for leasing of aircraft. The Committee recommends and directs that a market oriented
 transparent tender process should be formulated for leasing of aircraft either for short term or long term arrangements.
 
INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED
(Recommendation at 
Para 32)
 
22.       The Committee notes that there is a scope for further improvement in the overall load factor of Indian Airlines
 and recommends that there is a need to focus attention of all the factors that are responsible for acting as constraints in
 the achievement of the desired level of overall load factor.   The Committee also notes with concern that the market
 share of national carriers has decreased despite the overall increase in the growth rate of domestic passengers' traffic,
 which is also reflected in the decline in the reported profits of Indian Airlines.  The Committee recommends that
 adequate steps, in addition to the acquisition of aircraft, should be taken to enable Indian Airlines to tap the market
 opportunities in the domestic as well as international markets.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
23.       Overall Load Factor of Indian Airlines in the past few years has shown an increasing trend as can be seen from
 the statistics provided below:-
 
 
      Period
           Load Factor (%)
2003-04                 65.4
2004-05              68.6
2005-06              71.4
 
24.       Capacity share of Indian Airlines in the domestic market has been declining with the induction of capacity by the
 competitors and due to the reason that Indian Airlines has not been able to match its competitors in this regard.  
 Consequently IA’s market share has also tended to decline.    Airlines the world over experience a similar direct
 correlation between their capacity share and market share.   Indian Airlines has made efforts to retain its capacity share
 by leasing of aircraft pending renewal/augmentation of fleet through outright purchase route.  The aircraft that Indian
 Airlines has leased in the recent years have largely served to replace some of the aging A300 aircraft that have been
 phased out by the airline during this period.

25.       Due to inordinate delay in the finalization of IA’s fleet acquisition programme the average age of IA’s fleet
 compares quite unfavourably with that of its competitors’.    The travelling public perceive an older aircraft to be an
 inferior product and consequently IA's services have not been quite as appealing to some of the passengers and as such
 they prefer the services offered by IA's competitors.   
 
26.       Indian Airlines takes continuous measures to improve its services and product offered to its passengers.   Some
 of the measures taken to improve services and product upgrades are as follows:-
-
          Schedule upgrades and capacity increases.
-          Special fares/schemes on the Domestic sectors and dynamic market fares as well as incentives on
 international sectors.
-          Sales and marketing initiatives.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
27.       The Committee notes that despite increase in the overall load factor, market share of the Indian Airlines has gone
 down.  The Committee hopes that after acquisition of fleet, the share of Indian Airlines in the market will also improve.
 
(Recommendation at 
Para 34)
 
28.       The Committee feels that the issue of wage revision of employees of Indian Airlines has been pending for a long
 time. In this connection, the Committee would like to draw the attention of the Ministry to the recommendations made
 by the Committee in its 96
th Report, which is reproduced below: -
 
“The Committee expresses its anguish over the evasive comments of the Ministry offered in response to the
 recommendation of the Parliamentary Committee.  The Committee is extremely unhappy about the lackadaisical
 approach of the Ministry on the issue of revision of scales of pay of employees of Indian Airlines.  The
 Committee is of the view that the satisfaction level of the personnel in the matter of service conditions is a
 major factor affecting the performance of any organisation.  The total inaction on the part of the Ministry in the
 matter of pay revision of employees of Indian Airlines is surprising, especially in the present age of poaching
 and stiff competition by other Indian scheduled carriers.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates that the Ministry
 should expedite its decision in the matter in the overall interest of the employees and the organisation.”   The
 Committee once again reiterates the above recommendation and expects an early action thereon.

 providing reliable schedule services on regional routes.  It is not possible to provide reliable schedule services on metro
 routes with 5 aircraft.  It is believed that more than 10 aircraft would be needed to provide reliable schedule services on
 metro routes.  For international operations the operator must have a proper network for providing services within India
 on metro, regional and sub-regional routes.  It was in this context that it was considered essential that an airline, which

Para 121)
 
87.       The Committee observes that oflate there have been changes in the strategy of private airlines operators by way
 of consolidation of their operations.  The Committee feels that these conditions can lead to monopolistic situation in
 civil aviation sector and there is a need to check this trend.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that while
 formulating the new Civil Aviation Policy, all the consequences of merger of airlines including the matter regarding
 reallocation of infrastructural facilities at airports should be addressed properly.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
88.       Merger, takeovers etc. of airlines is part of the process of industry consolidations and is in line with global trends
 in the developed aviation market. The Government’s intent is to adopt a non-discriminatory approach towards all
 airlines, not to cause public inconvenience by disruption of flight schedules and to adopt a policy that would not be
 arbitrary and would not hamper growth and consolidation of airline industry.  Based on these considerations, a policy to
 be followed regarding use of Airport Infrastructure in case of merger/takeover of airlines and sale/transfer of aircraft
 has been approved in this Ministry and has been published on its web site.
 
89.       As regards the observation on likely monopolistic situation arising due to acquisition/merger, the same fall under
 the purview of Competition Commission/MRTPC.  Ministry of Civil Aviation is in favour of encouraging healthy
 competition in the aviation sector so that passengers have greater choices for travel at reasonable tariffs.
 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
90.       The Committee notes that the Ministry of Civil Aviation have framed a policy regarding use of Airport
 Infrastructure in case of merger/takeover of airlines and sale/transfer of aircraft. The Committee hopes that the policy
 will encourage a healthy competition in Civil Aviation Sector which in turn benefit the passengers.

Recommendation at

91.       The Committee is surprised to note that no final decision has been taken by the Ministry to review the existing
 Routes Dispersal Guidelines although the internal Committee set up under the Chairmanship of Director General of
 Civil Aviation had submitted its report on 18
th March 2005. The Committee also notes that although no decision has
 been taken on the proposal to impose a surcharge to fund the minimum subsidy to be given to the successful bidder
 who offers to operate in North Eastern region, island territories and the States of Jammu & Kashmir, the proposal was
 initiated on the demands made by airlines operators for amending/scrapping of the Route Dispersal Guidelines as they
 find it uneconomical to operate to the said regions on purely commercial considerations.  The Committee is of the view
 that the demands of the private operators are unjustified as the national carriers are also operating to the said regions on
 purely social considerations. The Committee is of the opinion that the private carriers should also share the social
 obligations.  In view of the boom in the domestic passenger traffic, the Committee feels that the hitherto non-
commercial or unviable routes have been transformed into profit making routes.  The Committee recommends that the

 Ministry should also make a study as to whether the grant of minimum subsidy to airline operators will result in
 corresponding reduction in airfares on the main routes.

 compliance of route dispersal guidelines issued by Government. The recommendations of the Committee under the
 Chairmanship of Director General of Civil Aviation for reviewing existing guidelines as well as other alternative
 strategies to facilitate connectivity to different region of the country including North East is under consideration of the
 Government.   It may be mentioned that there has been significant growth in the domestic aviation sector in the

The Ministry of Civil Aviation is responsible for the formulation of national policies and programmes for the
 development and regulation of civil aviation in the country and for devising and implementing schemes for orderly
 growth and expansion of civil air transport.  Its functions also extend to overseeing the provision of airport facilities, air
 traffic services, carriage of passengers and goods by air, safeguarding civil aviation operations, regulation of air
 transport services, licensing of aerodromes, air carriers, pilots and aircraft maintenance engineers. In addition to
 framing policies, the Ministry provides guidance to the organisations in the implementation of policy guidelines. It
 supervises implementation by the organisations of special programmes of the Government, particularly those intended
 for weaker sections.  The Ministry also administratively controls the Commission of Railway Safety, a statutory body

 yield a positive result in its profits and an increase in the passenger load factor in the ensuing years.

 that Air India should adopt an aggressive marketing strategy to face the stiff competition at global level. The
 Committee is also of the opinion that more passenger friendly amenities be provided in its aircraft so that more and

 Annual Plan 2006-07.  The Ministry in its reply stated that the main reason for variation is on account of the fact that
 the Annual Plan was made with the projection that 6 aircraft (out of the 43 aircraft) will be received in 2006-07,
 however, as per the revised delivery schedule, only one new aircraft was scheduled to join in 2006-07, and the same
 (A-319) has already joined in the fleet in October'06.  The difference on this account is Rs.347.71 crore.  The Ministry
 has also stated the remaining difference of Rs.8.29 crore is on account of taking up only essential and operationally
 necessary projects during the year, exchange rate variation and payments made to IGRUA.

 acquisition of new aircraft for Indian Airlines.  The Ministry replied that the Government had approved a proposal for
 acquisition of 43 Airbus aircraft, fitted with CFM engines, for Indian Airlines, at an estimated net project cost of
 Rs.9888 crore.  An agreement was executed with Airbus Industries and CFM International on 20.02.2006 in the
 presence of the Prime Minister and the President of France.  These aircraft are scheduled to be delivered between
 October, 2006 to March 2010.  The first A-319 was delivered on 19.10.2006 and the remaining aircraft would be
 delivered at the rate of one aircraft per month from June, 2007 to June, 2009 (except September, 2007).  The aircraft
 delivery during the period of July 2009 to March, 2010 would take place at the rate of two aircraft per month.  On
 induction of new aircraft, the old fleet of A-300 and B-737-200 would be replaced in a phased manner.

 aircraft/engine manufacturers during 2007-08. This would only meet a part of the complete acquisition cost of Indian
 Airlines.  The total acquisition cost is 10,169 crore and the balance payments for the new aircraft would be made in
 subsequent years.

 exercise capacity and entry of new players in the market.   However, the overall load factor has seen a substantial
 increased from 69.01% in the year 2004-05 to 71.6% in the year 2005-06. 
26.       The Committee notes that even though there is a substantial increase in the passenger load factor for the period
 from April to September, 2006, the profit of the IA seems to be declining. The physical performance of the Indian

27.       The Committee hopes that induction of new aircraft will help Indian Airlines to improve its profitability and the

MERGER OF AIR INDIA LIMITED AND INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED
46.       The Ministry was specifically asked about the merger of Air India and Indian Airlines Ltd.  In its response, the
 Ministry has stated that the Government has decided to merge the two airlines into a new company, which would
 further strengthen the public sector airlines.  The new airline would be the largest airline in the country comparable to
 other airlines in Asia and will provide an integrated international and national footprint.   The merger would enable
 these two airlines to pool their resources, achieve synergies, face competition and establish fresh benchmarks for
 efficiency and reliability.   The merger of the two airlines would be completed in a phased manner over the next two
 years.
47.       The Ministry has also stated that the merger is in keeping with the industry trend of moving towards
 consolidation and mergers enabling the airlines to achieve synergies and reduce costs.  The merged airline would be
 able to offer an integrated schedule from interior points in the country(currently served by Indian) to various
 international destinations (currently served by Indian and/or Air India) and vice-versa, offering seamless connectivity to
 passengers and also extending the connectivity of interior points to various international destinations via the major hub
 airports in India. 
48.       A bigger and stronger public sector national carrier will also help in expanding regional connectivity to hitherto
 under-serviced and un-serviced destinations.   While taking the merger decision, employees interests have been
 accorded prime importance.   The Government is committed to ensure that all legitimate interests of employee,
 including their current compensations, status, etc. are protected.   There will be no retrenchment and all employees of
 both the airlines will continue in the merged company.  The exercise of integrating manpower would be completed in a
 phased manner, on the basis of transparent and objective criteria.  A well-defined Grievance Redressal Machinery will
 also be put in place.
49.       The Committee raised the question on the issue of extra expenditure to be incurred on completing the process on
 which the Secretary, stated as under:
"Sir, there would be cost of the integration merger.   But the consultants have given a roadmap which indicates that on
 balance, there would a saving because there would be savings in terms of synergies, savings in terms of avoidance of
 duplication, etc.  So, at the end of the third year, there would be a saving of Rs.400 crore, taking into account the extra
 costs involved in the higher pay scales, etc".
50.       The Committee also expressed its concern over the issue of positioning of employees of both the carriers in the
 new entity for which the Secretary stated as under:
"Sir, I would be less than honest if I say that there will be no problems.  The HR issues in any merger cause problems,
 and when you have two large entities with 18,000 plus employees and 15,000 plus employees, it certainly not going to
 be an easy task.  But apart from the fact that there will be no retrenchment and nobody would lose his job and so which
 is the most basis thing, what the employees have been assured is that there will be a three-tier grievance redressal
 machinery which will be put in place..."

UNIFORM TAXATION OF ATF     
66.       During the course of the oral evidence of the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Committee was
 informed that the domestic air transport industry of the nation has been facing serious problems due to high costs of
 operations. One of the major reasons for this is the heavy cost of Air Turbine Fuel (ATF).  Even though the pricing of
 ATF is now on import parity basis, the rates applicable for domestic operations continue to be significantly higher than
 that of international operations.  The cost of ATF goes up even further due to high rates of sales tax levied by the State
 Governments/Union Territory Administration varying from 25 per cent to 30 per cent which affects the viability of
 domestic airline operations.
67.       The Secretary, while tendering his evidence also raised this issue  before the Committee  and stated as under:
".....Sir, as you aware, is a very important and a major component of the variable cost of operations.   Sir, the cost in
 India, the way it is priced and the way there is excise duty and , then there is Sales Tax in the States, is much higher, at
 least 25-30 per cent higher than what it is overseas.  We have been requesting that at least it be notified as a declared
 good under section 14 of the Central Sales Tax Act for all types of aircraft; so that there is a cap on the quantum of levy
 which can be imposed on this.  Sir, presently it is four per cent; ...... we have got some relief in relation to smaller
 aircraft, but it is not yet available for the aviation sector and all the operators, as a whole".
 
68.       The Ministry was asked about the budget proposal to amend the Central Sales Tax to treat aviation turbine fuel
 as a declare goods for all small aircraft with a maximum take of less than 40,000 kg operated by scheduled carriers and
 also the impact of this amendment on the aviation sector for which the ministry replied that until now, this facility was
 available only to turbo-prop aircraft.   The present proposal to extend the concession to all small aircraft including jet
 aircraft operated by scheduled airlines would encourage and facilitate connectivity to non-metro and other smaller cities
 by more efficient small jet aircraft.
 
69.       The Cost of fuel is an important component of cost structure and has direct bearing on the profitability of any
 airline. High cost of ATF in the country increases the cost of operation of carriers which results in escalation in the
 airfares.  The Committee recommends that Ministry of Finance should sympathetically consider and give approval to
 the proposal of Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding notifying ATF as 'Declared Good' under Section 14 of Central
 Sales Tax Act on priority basis to all the aircraft  so that sales tax on ATF could be contained with the maximum rate of
 4%. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Finance may also discuss the issue with the State
 Governments and try to pursuade them to reduce   the sales tax on ATF.  The Committee feels that restructuring the
 excise duty on ATF will have a positive impact on the development of civil aviation sector of the nation.
UTILISATION OF CAT III SYSTEM AT DELHI AIRPORT
70.       During the winter season, the air passengers are put into great hardship by cancellation/diversion of flights due
 to fog at Delhi airport.  The Committee sought the remedial actions proposed to avoid such a situation during the next
 year. The Ministry in its reply stated that the airlines are encouraged to upgrade their aircraft and train their pilots for
 operations in low visibility conditions.   Their flight schedules are approved on the basis of number of pilots trained by
 the operators for low visibility operations and the suitability of the planes for such operations.   If the operator cannot
 provide data for their capability to fly under low visibility, they are not allowed to schedule their flights during normal
 fog hours.  The Ministry also stated that airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III trained pilots on
 international routes during the fog season.  DGCA also requires that the airlines should train their pilots for ILS CAT
 II/III operations.   Pilots who are CAT II/III qualified are approved as Instructor/Examiner so as to ensure that more
 trained pilots are available for CAT II/III operations during low visibility conditions. 
71.       The Committee is constrained to note that a huge investment has been made in installation of ILS CAT-III
 facilities at IGI airport.  However there is a lot of delay or cancellation of flights due to fog as there are not enough
 pilots trained to operate the flights during fog. It appears that steps taken by the Government in this regard have proved
 inadequate. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that Airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III
 trained pilots on international routes during fog season and also recommended that  training of pilots to fly on low
 visibility conditions be extended to a maximum number of pilots in both the national carriers. The Committee
 recommends that strict penal provisions should be imposed on the airlines which are failing to give proper training to

 substantial amount of money has been spent by the AAI for repair and maintenance work at international airports at
 Delhi and Mumbai even after these two airports were handed over to the JVCs in May, 2006.  The Committee desires
 to know the reasons for this and also wants to know the expenditure incurred by the JVCs on the respective airports for
 maintenance and up keep of airports till date.
            A Tripartite Committee with the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, Airports Authority of India and
 AAI Employees Joint Forum has been constituted by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on     22
nd February, 2006 to look
 into the issues and proposals of modernizing airports by Airports Authority of India and employees related issues
 including job security.  The Committee desires to know the details of meetings which have been taken so far with the
 decisions arrived therein.  The Committee also reiterates its recommendation contained in its 106
th Report that the
 Tripartite Committee should hold regular meetings and finalise its Report in a time bound manner in view of the
 importance of the issues relating to the Committee.

            There are also reports that after the work of modernisation of Delhi and Mumbai Airports has gone in the hands
 of private operators, the Ministry of Tourism even finding difficult to have space at the airports to display the publicity
 materials meant for information of the tourists particularly coming from abroad.  This gives an impression that there is
 a lack of coordination between the private operators and the Government agencies.  The Committee recommends that
 Government should look into the matter and take remedial action to ensure that Ministry of Tourism and other agencies
 which have to work at the airports to provide amenities to the passengers and tourist in particular do not face any
 problem.                    (Paras 56, 57, 58)       
CHENNAI AND KOLKATA AIRPORTS
 
            The Committee is constrained to note that the indecisiveness is preventing with regard to modernisation of
 Kolkata and Chennai Airport as Government is yet to give its approval for modernisation plans of these two Airports.
 The Committee recommends that the modernisation of Chennai and Kolkata airports should be completed on priority so
 as to ease the traffic over Delhi and Mumbai airports.  The Committee also desires that both these airports may be
 developed as international hubs to cater the needs of the people in the eastern and southern part of the country.  The
 Committee hopes that the Airports Authority of India will complete the all modernisation and developmental works of
 Kolkata and Chennai airports within a specified time frame.(Para 62)
SHORTAGE AND TRAINING OF PILOTS
            The Committee hopes that modernization of IGRUA and establishment of new pilot training institute in Gondia
 will help to meet the shortage of pilots. The Committee recommends that more training institute like that of the
 proposed one of the Gondia may also be established at conspicuous places in the Northern, Eastern and Southern parts
 of the country to meet the shortage of Pilots. (Para 65)
UNIFORM TAXATION OF ATF
The Cost of fuel is an important component of cost structure and has direct bearing on the profitability of any airline.
 High cost of ATF in the country increases the cost of operation of carriers which results in escalation in the airfares. 
 The Committee recommends that Ministry of Finance should sympathetically consider and give approval to the
 proposal of Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding notifying ATF as 'Declared Good' under Section 14 of Central Sales
 Tax Act on priority basis to all the aircraft   so that sales tax on ATF could be contained with the maximum rate of 4%.
 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Finance may also discuss the issue with the State
 Governments and try to pursuade them to reduce   the sales tax on ATF.  The Committee feels that restructuring the
 excise duty on ATF will have a positive impact on the development of civil aviation sector of the nation. (Para 69)
UTILISATION OF CAT III SYSTEM AT DELHI AIRPORT
            The Committee is constrained to note that a huge investment has been made in installation of ILS CAT-III
 facilities at IGI airport.  However there is a lot of delay or cancellation of flights due to fog as there are not enough
 pilots trained to operate the flights during fog. It appears that steps taken by the Government in this regard have proved
 inadequate. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that Airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III
 trained pilots on international routes during fog season and also recommended that  training of pilots to fly on low
 visibility conditions be extended to a maximum number of pilots in both the national carriers. The Committee
 recommends that strict penal provisions should be imposed on the airlines which are failing to give proper training to
 their pilots in the upgraded instrument landing systems.  The Committee hopes that incidents of cancellation of flights
 during the winter season in 2007 will be minimum.(Para 71)

10.       The Committee is distressed to note that during the 10 th Plan, the Department of Shipping was allocated Rs.2570.89
 crore as budgetary allocation under the plan scheme which was reduced to Rs.1700.00 crore at the RE stage. The Committee
 does not see any merit therein and strongly disapproves the idea of reduction of plan outlay because once it is reduced by the
 Government at the beginning of the Five Year Plan itself it will certainly affect and jeopardise many of the plan activities of
 the Department. The Committee is further constrained to note the shortfall in utilization of funds in almost all the major
 activities of Department of Shipping i.e. Inland Water Transport, Shipping, Ports, Lighthouses and Lightships, Shipbuilding
 etc. During 2005-06, the utilization of funds was Rs.346.83 crore against RE Rs.405.00 crore, in 2006-07, the utilization of
 funds was Rs.510.21 crore against RE Rs.575.00 crore and Rs.759.00 crore has been allocated for BE 2007-08. The
 Committee is aware that the main reason for effecting reduction in funds at RE stage by the Ministry of Finance is the inability
 of the Department of Shipping to spend their allocated funds during the first two quarters of almost every  year.  The
 Committee observes that the major portions of the budgetary outlay had been utilized during the last two quarters of the
 financial year by the Department. The Committee disapproves the practice as the funds crucial for the development of
 Shipping and Port Sectors infrastructure are withheld in the process. The Committee notes that the reasons advanced by the
 Department for non-utilization are administrative in nature for which corrective action could have been taken in advance. The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to plan and incur their expenditure in a proportionate manner so that it is
 evenly spread throughout the year so that the funds are utilised appropriately for the purposes and no alibi should be provided
 to the Ministry of Finance to reduce the allocations at the RE stage.

TONNAGE TAX REGIME
36.       The Government has rationalized the fiscal regime for Indian Shipping Industry by introducing Tonnage Tax system
 from the financial year 2004-05, in order to provide Indian Shipping industry a level playing field vis-à-vis International
 shipping companies and also facilitate the growth of Indian tonnage. In response to introduction of Tonnage tax regime and
 also due to current shipping boom, Indian Tonnage has steadily grown in the last about 2 years. Indian tonnage as on
 01.06.2004 was 7.05 million Gross Tonnage (GT) which has increased to 8.42 million GT as on 03.12.2006. Dredgers have
 also been included in the Tonnage Tax regime as per Finance Act 2005-06.
37.       Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country do not have the critical mass to compete with the
 other mode of transport on its own and for its development requires fiscal support from the Government. The Committee in its
 105
th Report on Demands for Grants for 2006-07 of the Department of Shipping had recommended for inclusion of the vessels
 registered under Inland Vessels and Coastal Vessels Acts in the tonnage tax regime for development of the Inland Water
 Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country. The Committee wanted to know about the progress made in the matter.
 The Department of Shipping in their written reply submitted that in the current year also the Department had taken up the
 matter with Ministry of Finance on various occasions, for inclusion of vessels registered under Indian Vessel Act and Coastal
 Vessel Act, under tonnage tax regime.  It was emphasized that these vessels are adversely affected as Section 33 AC benefit,
 which was available to them till 2003-04 (before introduction of tonnage tax) was withdrawn without extending the tonnage
 tax benefits.   However, this issue has not figured in the Budget of 2007-08 presented by Hon’ble Finance Minister in the
 Parliament.
38.       The Committee notes that with the introduction of the Tonnage Tax system and other fiscal incentives the Indian
 shipping companies have registered the growth of the Indian tonnage. However, the Committee is constrained to note that the
 vessels registered under the   Indian Vessels Act, 1917 and the Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 have not been included for the
 purpose of getting tonnage tax benefits. The Committee feels that Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the
 country do not have the critical mass to compete with the other mode of transport on its own and for its development requires
 fiscal support from the Government. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department to impress upon the Ministry of
 Finance for extending the benefits of tonnage tax to these vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act and Coastal Vessels
 Act so as to harness the IWT potential in the country.
CRUISE SHIPPING
39.       Cruise shipping is a fast growing sector globally. As a departure from the concept of cargo and passenger ships, cruise
 is like a moving township studded with all state of art facilities including all types of recreational activities. The idea is fast
 catching because journey on cruise is not only pleasurable, but also comparatively free from sea travel health hazards. The
 global scenario for cruise shipping is picking up very fast, with an annual increment from 10-20% in the cruise ship fleet and
 passengers carried. Experience in the Caribbean, Latin American and South-East Asian countries indicate that huge amount of
 foreign exchange can be earned by providing the right policy environment and infrastructure for the growth of cruise shipping.
 India with its vast and beautiful coastline, virgin forests and undisturbed idyllic islands, long historical and cultural tradition of
 architecture, theatre and performing arts can be a fabulous tourist destination. With a view to encourage cruise shipping in the
 country, Government is considering to bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy.
40.       The Committee wanted to know from the Department of Shipping about the progress made for development of
 infrastructure and other facilities for development of cruise shipping in both eastern and western coasts of the country. The
 Department of Shipping intimated that in order to promote cruise tourism, a Cruise Shipping Policy is under consideration of
 the Government.   The objective of the policy is to make India a major cruise destination by popularizing cruise shipping,
 facilitating creation of requisite infrastructure by creating a conducive environment.   Phased programme will be evolved for
 development of facilities at ports for cruise shipping. The development of cruise tourism infrastructure is to be done through
 port resources, financial support from Ministry of Tourism under their scheme for promoting tourism as well as private sector

 investment.  Private sector participation will be encouraged for the development of cruise tourism infrastructure, wherever
 viable.   Moreover, 100% FDI is already permitted in shipping sector.  Guidelines exist permitting Private Sector participation
 in ports including cruise terminals.

 following steps have been taken and are being taken to encourage cruise shipping:
 
(i)                  A High Power Steering Group has been set up with a view to catalyze the growth and development of cruise
 shipping in India.
 
(ii)        Cabotage has been relaxed for cruise ships for a period of 5 years from December, 2003.
 
(iii)       Upto 50% rebate has been given in vessel related charges including  berth hire, pilotage, etc.
 
(iv)
              Phased programme will be evolved for development of facilities at ports for cruise shipping.
 
(v)
                100% FDI is already permitted in shipping sector.
 
(vi)              Systems and procedures are being streamlined to facilitate seamless travel of the tourists.
 
(vii)             Cruise operator M/s. Ocean Cruises India Pvt. Ltd. has been permitted to operate cruises from Goa to
 Lakshadweep via Cochin. Similarly Cruise operator M/s. Star Cruises has been             permitted to operate

 that in order to encourage the cruise shipping in the country, the Department has provided incentives to encourage private
 sector participation for development of cruise tourism facilities at ports on Eastern as well Western coasts. The Committee

RECOUPMENT OF SEAMEN’S PROVIDENT FUND
 
50.       The Seamen’s Provident Fund Scheme, 1966 framed under the Seamen's Provident Fund Act, 1966 was introduced
 retrospectively with effect from 1
st July 1964 to provide a provident fund for all seamen in view of obvious need to provide old
 age retirement benefits to seamen and to their family members in the event of the death. This was a contributory Provident
 Fund and the employees were required to deposit the Provident Fund contributions in respect of Seamen employed by them
 with their matching contribution with Seamen's Provident Fund Organisation after the terminations of each voyage.  All money
 belonging to the Funds were invested in the Securities as per the pattern prescribed by the Ministry of Finance. As on 31
st
 December, 2006, the Organization is holding 34,931 accounts and the total amount of provident fund accumulations (including
 interest) is Rs.529,57,96,164/- this also includes an amount of Rs. 90,15,57,516,.17/- at risk due to securities scam, which
 came to notice in May, 2002.
 
51.       The Committee in its earlier Reports had recommended for recouping the shortage of an amount of Rs.92.78 crore in the
 Seamen Provident Funds. The Committee wanted to know from the Department of Shipping about the progress made in the
 matter so far, the Department of Shipping informed that the Government has approved the proposal in its meeting held on
 30.11.2006 to recoup the full amount of Rs. 92.78 crore in the Seamen’s Provident Fund. As per decision of the Government ,
 action is being taken to introduce a Bill to amend the Seamen’s Provident Fund Act 1966 with a view to distancing in

file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/117thReport.htm[22-10-2018 12:22:07]
 sequencing  the Government from the responsibility of the Fund in future and to  release the grant to Seamen’s Provident Fund.
52.       The Secretary, the Department of Shipping during the course of the oral evidence apprised the Committee that:
 
“Sir, you have mentioned about Seamen’s Provident Fund.  You will be happy to note that after great persuasion, the
 Group of Ministers have finally recommended and the Cabinet has finally decided that Rs.92 crore, which were mis-
invested, would be reimbursed by the Government.  So, this is a very great decision of the Government of India.  But
 the Ministry of Finance said that before releasing this money, there must be a legislation in the Parliament that in such
 situations, the liabilities arising out of Seamen’s Provident Fund investment should not create liabilities for the
 Government and institutions should go in the same manner for other public sectors.  We have written to the Parliament
 also informing our intention to introduce the Bill.  I think, in the coming next half of the Budget Session, this will be
 introduced, and, we will get that money by the end of May.”
 
53.       The Committee is happy to note that as per its recommendations, the Government has approved the proposal for
 recoupment of Rs.92.78 crore in the Seamen’s Provident Fund. The Committee also notes that in order to ensure that such
 happenings are not repeated in future, a Bill to amend the Seamen’s Provident Fund Act, 1966 and to release the grant to
 Seamen’s Provident Fund is under consideration. However, the Committee disapproves the idea of linking the proposal for
 recoupment of Rs.92.78 crore with the amendment of Seamen’s Provident Fund Act. Because misappropriation of the amount
 belonging to the seamen was due to faulty rules/policy of the Government due to which the poor seamen were the sufferers.

68.       Inland waterways comprising of rivers, lakes, canals, creeks, backwaters etc extend to about 14500 km in the country.
