TONNAGE TAX REGIME
49.       With the rationalization of the fiscal regime for Indian Shipping Industry and introduction of Tonnage Tax system from the financial year 2004-05, the Government has provided Indian Shipping industry a level playing field vis-à-vis International shipping companies and also facilitated the growth of Indian tonnage. In response to introduction of Tonnage
 tax regime and also due to current shipping boom, Indian Tonnage now stand at 9.04 million GT as on 31.12.2007 with 850 vessels. The Dredgers have also been included in the Tonnage Tax regime as per Finance Act 2005-06.
50.       The Committee has been informed by the stakeholders that Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country do not have the critical mass to compete with the other mode of transport on its own and for its development and requires fiscal support from the Government. The Committee in its various Reports on Demands for Grants of the
 Department of Shipping had recommended for inclusion of the vessels registered under Inland Vessels and Coastal Vessels Acts in the tonnage tax regime for development of the Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country. The Committee wanted to know about the progress made in the matter. The Department of Shipping in their written
 reply submitted that the Department of Shipping has been taking up the matter with Ministry of Finance at various levels from the year 2005-06 requesting them to include the vessels registered under Inland Vessels Act and Coasting Vessel Act in the Tonnage tax regime.   Ministry of Finance was again requested in November, 2005, August,2006 and August,
 2007.  This matter was discussed with Ministry of Finance in January, 2008.  During the discussion, the point came up that tonnage tax would not be beneficial to loss making units like CIWTC as they would be burdened with tonnage tax unnecessarily. 
51.       The Committee is not satisfied with the repeated replies of the Department.  The Committee feels that worthwhile action should have been taken by the Government on the specific recommendation of the Committee for inclusion of vessels registered under the   Indian Vessels Act, 1917 and the Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 for getting tonnage tax benefits for
 the development of the Inland Water Transport and Coastal Vessel Transport in the country.  The Committee apprehends that the Government does not desire to rationalize the fiscal regime for Indian Shipping Industry for facilitating the growth of the Indian tonnage.  The Committee disapproves the contention of the Department that introduction of tonnage tax
 to these vessels would unnecessarily burdened the CIWTC. The Committee desires the Department to conduct a feasibility study to know the profit-loss benefits with the introduction of tonnage tax regime to these vessels and submit a report to the Committee. 
CRUISE SHIPPING
52.       India with its vast and beautiful coastline, virgin forests and undisturbed idyllic islands, long historical and cultural tradition of architecture, theatre and performing arts can be a fabulous tourist destination. The global scenario for cruise shipping is picking up very fast, with an annual increment from 10-20% in the cruise ship fleet and passengers carried.
 As a departure from the concept of cargo and passenger ships, cruise is like a moving township studded with all state of art facilities including all types of recreational activities. The idea is fast catching because journey on cruise is not only pleasurable, but also comparatively free from sea travel health hazards. Experience in the Caribbean, Latin American and
 South-East Asian countries indicate that huge amount of foreign exchange can be earned by providing the right policy environment and infrastructure for the growth of cruise shipping. With a view to encourage cruise shipping in the country, Government is considering to bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy.
53.       The Committee in its 117
th Report on Demands for Grants (2007-08) of the Department of Shipping has dealt with the subject and recommended the Government to formulate a policy for development of cruise shipping in the country.  The Committee enquired the Department about the status of formulation of cruise shipping policy for popularizing cruise
 shipping and development of infrastructure facilities in the country,  the Department of Shipping in their replies submitted that Draft Policy on Cruise Shipping has been under preparation since 28.09.2004 when the High Powered Steering Group under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister (S & RTH) and Co-chaired by Hon’ble Minister of tourism & Culture
 was set up.  As decided in the meeting of High Powered Steering Group, different working Groups were set up to examine issues like immigration, Custom clearance,  Infrastructure at Ports, Taxation, connectivity etc.   Based on the reports of Working Groups, a Draft Cruise Shipping Policy was considered by the High Powered Group in its meeting held on
 6.12.2006.  While there was a consensus about the proposed policy, it was decided that the issue relating to river cruise and environment be also addressed and the matter to include cruise shipping in the LTC be taken up with Ministry of Finance.  Accordingly, a meeting was held on 26 th March, 2007 under the Chairmanship of Secretary (Shipping) to consider
 the issue relating to river cruise and to address environmental matters for inclusion in the draft cruise shipping policy.   The matter was referred to Ministry of Environment and Forests, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Tourism and Director (IWAI) for their comments.   Based on their comments, a Draft Cabinet Note was
 circulated to the concerned Ministries/Departments on 12th September, 2007 for their views.  The views of appraisal agencies have been received, the latest being from Planning Commission on 31.12.2007.  These are under examination.  The comprehensive cruise shipping policy is likely to be finalized in another two months. 
54.       As regards attracting investments from private sector including FDI with a view to develop infrastructure and other facilities for development of cruise  shipping in the country, the Department of Shipping informed that the High Power Steering Group       (HPSG) under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister (SRT&H) with the Union Minister of Tourism
 and Culture as Co-Chairperson was set up to formulate a Cruise Shipping Policy with the objective of making   India a major cruise destination by popularizing Cruise Shipping, facilitating creation of requisite infrastructure and creating a conducive environment.   The Govt. has already allowed 100% FDI in shipping sector including Cruise Shipping. Similarly,
 investment from private sector is also allowed on PPP basis. The draft Cruise Shipping policy provides for development of cruise facilities in the ports in a phased manner. The policy is under finalization in consultation with the concerned Ministries.
55.       The Committee is concerned that despite its recommendations in the earlier reports on Demands for Grants urging the Government to bring out a comprehensive cruise shipping policy, the Government neither complied with its recommendations nor formulated the cruise shipping policy till date although it has been informed by the Department on
 09.01.2008 that the comprehensive cruise shipping policy will be formulated within a period of two months.  The Committee feels that in the absence of a comprehensive cruise shipping policy the Department will not be able to popularize the cruise shipping and address all the aspect of facilitating creation of infrastructure, encourage investments from the
 private sector and create a congenial and hospitable environment for growth of cruise shipping in the country.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates its earlier recommendation urging the Government to bring out a comprehensive policy on cruise shipping without further delay.

INLAND WATER TRANSPORT
76.       Inland waterways comprising of rivers, lakes, canals, creeks, backwaters, etc. extend to about 14,500 kms. in India.  However, the true potential of this important mode of transport is yet to be exploited.
77.       Inland Water Transport (IWT) schemes mainly relate to development of waterways and augmentation of the traffic carrying capacity through expansion and modernization of IWT infrastructure/vessels.   Whereas the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) is responsible for the development of National Waterways, responsibility for the development
 of State Waterways rests with the State Governments. The Central Government has declared three Waterways, viz. Allahabad  – Haldia Stretch (1620 Kms.) Sadiya and Dhubri Stretch (891 kms.) and West Coast Canal from Kollam to Kottapuram stretch along with Udyogamandal Champakara canals (205 kms.) as National Waterways  and are being developed
 by IWAI for shipping and navigation by providing/maintaining basic IWT infrastructure i.e. fairway, navigational aids and terminals.  Three more waterways namely the Kakinada-Puducherry canals along with Godavari and Krishna rivers (1095 km), East Coast Canal along with Brahmani river and Mahanadi  delta (623 km) and Barak river (121 km) are under
 active consideration of the Govt for declaration as new National Waterways.
78.       In BE 2007-08, an outlay of Rs.158 crore which included Rs.75.90 crore for North-Eastern areas and Rs.82.10 crore for grants to IWAI was provided to the IWT sector.  This was reduced to Rs.138.60 crore at RE stage and an expenditure upto Febuary 2008 is Rs.56.53 crore and the anticipated expenditure upto March 2008 is Rs.107.73 crore.  During the
 Financial Year 2008-09, a sum of Rs.180.00 crore (including Rs.60.00 crore for NE Pool) has been earmarked towards Plan Support to IWAI. 
79.       Inland Water Transport Policy framework and strategy for development including guidelines for private investment in IWT sector have been approved by the Government.  These measures aim at helping IWAI to mobilize the required resources by attracting Private Investment and by forming Joint Ventures for developing Waterway Infrastructure &
 Cargo handling facilities.  To achieve a substantial step-up in IWT traffic, the thrust will therefore, be on the creation of infrastructure in the form of fairways with adequate depth and width besides setting-up of terminals and navigational aids.  An Inland Vessel Building Subsidy Scheme for providing 30% Subsidy for Inland Vessels built in Indian Shipyard and
 for operation on National Waterways was in existence from 1
st April, 2002 to 31.03.2007.  It is proposed to extend it for 10 years beyond 31.03.2007.
80.          IWT traffic operations are predominantly controlled by private entrepreneurs, particularly in Goa region.  The only public sector undertaking in the IWT sector, Central Inland Water Transport Corporation (CIWTC) operates traffic in the Eastern and North Eastern Region. Approximate share of organized IWT sector in the country in terms of tonne-km
 is a little over 0.30% of the total inland freight transportation. IWAI had engaged M/s IFCI Ltd as a consultant for identifying and processing private sector participation projects in IWT field.   The consultant had prepared some priority projects which were advertised in the market inviting bids.  After due process of bidding four Memorandum of Understanding
 (MOU)’s have been signed between IWAI and respective successful bidders for setting up and management of jetties at Bandel, Kolaghat and Budge-Budge in West Bengal and for acquisition, operation and management of barges on O-D pairs of Kolkata-Mongla, Kolkata-Dhubri and Kolkata-Pandu.  This process was in line with IWT Policy, 2001. Further
 steps for setting up of JVs are being taken.  A project Development Organisation/ Project Development Committee mechanism for identifying, developing and processing PPP projects has been finalized.  Besides, one cement company has been given land at Pandu port for developing terminal for handling clinker, cement etc to be transported by IWT mode. 
 Institutional arrangements for development of IWT are already in place.   Inland Waterways Authority of India is a Central Government agency primarily responsible for development and regulation of National Waterways for shipping and navigation.   Most of the riverine States however, do not have separate organizations to look after IWT sector and need to
 build the same.  Also, wherever IWT organizations are available in the States, these also need to be up graded/ strengthened.  
81.       The Committee has consistently expressed its concern over the slow pace of utilization of plan outlays and development of Inland Water Transport sector in the country. The Committee notes with anguish that an outlay of Rs.158.00 crore was allocated in BE 2007-08 for the IWT sector but it was reduced to Rs.138.60 crore at RE stage and an expenditure
 of Rs.56.53 crore was made only upto February, 2008.   The Committee is disappointed to note the continuous under utilization of funds by the Department of Shipping for development of IWT sector.  The Committee expects that the Department would make every endeavour to ensure that the measures adopted for the growth of IWT sector in the country is
 monitored scrupulously to achieve the envisaged physical and financial targets. 
82.       The Committee notes that potential of the  Inland Water Transport remains largely unexplored due to the indifferent attitude of the Central and State Governments. The Committee observes that although the Department of Shipping is committed to increase the share of Inland Water Transport in the country’s total EXIM trade, still the waterways are not
 being utilized to their potential and remain largely neglected and underdeveloped for want of required infrastructure namely fairways, terminals and navigable aids, as a result, it has not reached at a threshold level to become commercially viable. The Committee is of the view that with adequate investments, policy framework and focused approach, the Inland
 Water Transport in the country can be developed into a viable transport mode complementary to the rail and road modes. The Committee is of the opinion that to develop the Inland Water Transport sector with fast pace to its full potential in the country, the Government should endeavor to provide institutional framework and minimize the procedural bottlenecks
 besides providing adequate investments both from public and private partnership primarily public investment in Inland Water Transport and to develop it to a level where private sector feels confident to invest in this sector particularly in ownership and operation of cargo and passenger vessels to Inland Water Transport mode. The Committee, therefore,
 recommends the Government to provide institutional framework and basic infrastructural facility for accelerated development of Inland Water Transport sector in the country under National Maritime Development Programme.

87.       The Committee wanted to know the reasons for the dropped centrally sponsored scheme for development of IWT Sector; the Department of Shipping informed the Committee that for good economic development of any country the transport infrastructure is an extremely important factor.  Primarily there are three modes of transportation for bulk goods
 namely Rail, Road and Inland Water Transport (IWT).  However, while the rail and road modes developed significantly in the country, the IWT mode remained totally neglected due to which this mode lost its significance in the overall transport mix.  The development of inland waterways started with the formation of Inland Waterways Authority of India
 (IWAI) in October 1986.  However, as per constitutional provisions, only those waterways which are declared as National Waterways by Acts of Parliament can be developed by the Central Govt/IWAI.  The other waterways remain under the purview of the respective State Government.
 88.       For overall development of IWT sector it is necessary that not only the National Waterways but the other waterways (many of which are the feeder waterways to these National Waterways) should also be developed by providing IWT infrastructure.  Then only the total potential of IWT sector
 in the country can be exploited.  The importance of development of this mode  assumes greater significance considering that the IWT mode is a cost effective, environment friendly and fuel efficient mode of transport, especially for bulk cargo, over dimensional cargo and hazardous cargo, if adequate infrastructure is developed and maintained on all potential
 waterways.
89.       Most of the State Governments, however, suffer from financial constraints due to which development of IWT mode does not become a priority activity for them.  It is because of this factor that a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) which existed till March 2002 under which 50% financial assistance had been provided by the Central Government to
 respective States as a loan on reimbursement basis.  However, due to the above nature of the financial assistance this scheme was not very popular among the States and therefore, the funding pattern of CSS for IWT sector was modified in 2002 (guidelines of revised CSS issued in Nov. 2002) and 100% grant for North Eastern States and 90% grant for other
 States of the country was made available for taking up projects for IWT development by the States under CSS for IWT sector.
90.       This change in funding pattern encouraged several States for taking up different projects for development of IWT mode and during the 10th Plan period alone, 35 projects of 15 States costing Rs.107 crore were sanctioned by the DoS and central share of Rs.53 crore was also released to these States during the years 2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06 and 2006-07.
(Annexure-II)
91.       However, Planning Commission during February, 2007, took a decision to discontinue this scheme.  For North Eastern sector, however, it was stated in Planning Commission’s letter no N-11016/5(1)/2006-PC dated 09.02.07 that the Central Sponsored Scheme for IWT development is converted into Central Sector Scheme. Due to the above decision of
 Planning Commission, the projects which were under implementation by different States got adversely affected and presently no new project is being considered by IWAI/DoS for sanction.  For North Eastern sector also the Central Sector Scheme is to be now implemented by DoS, projects will be technically evaluated by the IWAI and State governments will be
 the executing agencies. Guidelines for taking up these projects are being prepared by the DoS.
92.       Therefore, considering that the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for IWT development is very important for overall development of IWT sector in the country, IWAI has requested the DoS that the scheme may be revived for whole country as existed up to 31.03.07.  The Hon’ble Minister of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways has also requested the Dy.
 Chairman, Planning Commission as well as Hon’ble Prime Minister for continuation of this scheme vide letters dated 21.03.07 and 11.10.2007 respectively.
93.       The Committee notes with dismay over the discontinuance of the centrally sponsored scheme for IWT development in the country by the Planning Commission.  The Committee is of the view that the decision of the Planning Commission to convert the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for IWT development into central sector scheme will adversely
 affect the pace of development of Inland Water Transport in the country.  The Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to impress upon the Planning Commission for the revival of the central sponsored scheme for overall development of the IWT Sector during the annual plan itself.
94.       The Committee is constrained to note that cargo transportation by Inland Water Transport mode has not shown significant improvement on the three National Waterways.  The Committee also expresses its displeasure over the fact that no comparative cost-output evaluation for transportation of cargo through this inland water transport has been carried out
 by the Department.  The Committee is of the view that such evaluation would further establish the support of Inland Water Transport over other mode of transports.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that a detailed study should be carried out by the Department in this regard. The Committee also urges the Department to fix realistic physical target for cargo
 transportation by IWT mode year-wise for entire 11
th Plan period and put in place institutional monitoring mechanism for achieving the desired growth.
95.       Under the Trade Agreement entered into between the Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh and the Government of the Republic of India and the Protocol signed by both the countries on IWT Trade & Transit, IWAI is the nodal agency in issuing necessary permission for
 inland barges of Bangladesh and India for their movement across the country and undertaking loading/unloading operation at designated Ports of Call.  Checking of authorized/illegal transportation of men and materials (cargo) falls under the purview of Customs Department (for material) and Immigration Department (for men) and IWAI do not play any role in
 the same.  The above two authorities, at their respective check points, check and verify, if, the cargo carried by them and the men present on board the ship are as per the declared manifesto (certified by BIWTA, the nodal agency on Trade & Transit Protocol on behalf of Bangladesh Govt).  At all other points the Border Security Force keeps vigil on illegal
 immigrants/illegal movement of goods.  No security personnel is provided on Bangladeshi vessels by BSF/State Government/IWAI.  The crew of Bangladeshi vessels has to report to Customs and Immigration Department at their respective check points at the border for their verification and necessary entry.  Similarly, for outgoing vessels, the above details are
 again cross checked by Immigration/Customs Department.   The Government of West Bengal or Assam has never raised any issue regarding security problem due to plying of Bangladeshi vessels in Sunderbans/Protocol route.  Bangladeshi vessels never demanded from IWAI, security arrangement in their vessels nor have the State Government of West
 Bengal/Assam ever requested that security arrangement in Bangladeshi vessels be provided.  However, communications to the Government of West Bengal and Ministry of Home Affairs have been issued for comments in this regard. The reply is awaited.
96.       The Department of Shipping further informed that it is true that most of the transportation by IWT mode between Kolkata/ Haldia and Bangladesh  is by barges of Bangladesh flag.  However, on other routes i.e. Kolkata/ Haldia-Pandu and Kolkata/ Haldia- Karimganj, mostly Indian vessels are plying.  Reasons for Bangladesh vessels outnumbering Indian
 vessels on Kolkata/ Haldia- Narayanganj route are that Bangladeshi vessels are more economical in the tidal zone, they have lower cost of construction, less cost of manning and the bunker used by them is also cheaper. Though, there is a provision in the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol on Inland Water Transit and Trade for sharing of cargo on 50:50 basis by Indian
 and Bangladeshi flag vessels, it is very difficult to enforce the same in view of the market forces and limitation of availability of Indian flag vessels.  However, this point is being raised with the Bangladesh authorities as and when discussion takes place with them.
97.       The Committee notes with anguish that no security personnel are being provided for safe transportation of men and material in Suderbans/Protocol routes in West Bengal.   The Committee is of the opinion that security is a prime concern and should be looked into seriously by making commensurate security arrangement in Suderbans/Protocol routes.  The
 Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to take up the matter of beefing-up of security arrangement in the Suderbans/Protocol routes with the Union Home Ministry so that inadequacy of police deployment could be addressed in a big way.

98.       The Committee in its various reports on Demands for Grants of Department of Shipping had recommended for capital restructuring of CIWTC with its existing infrastructure, capacity and manpower and possibility to physically amalgamate the remaining CIWTC with Inland Waterway Authority of India (IWAI) or Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping
 Corporation of India (SCI), so that the infrastructure and expertise of CIWTC can be utilized for development of waterways transport.  The Department of Shipping in their Action Taken Replies inter-alia  informed the Committee that the possibilities of amalgamation or otherwise of this corporation with various Organizations, such as Inland Waterways
 Authority of India (IWAI), Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), was examined and not found feasible.  The Department of Shipping further informed that no feasibility study has been conducted for the physical amalgamation of the Corporation.
99.       The Department of Disinvestment has already initiated action to assess the viability of disinvestment of CIWTC with present and various employees’ number.  Notice for appointment of Consultant has been issued by the D/o Disinvestment.   Simultaneously, it has been decided to approach the Department of Disinvestment to share the consultant report
 with the Department of Shipping which will be examined independently in this Department.
100.     The Committee is pained to note that the Government has decided neither to consider revival of CIWTC nor to amalgamate this Corporation with various Organizations, such as Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) that too, without getting conducted any scientific study by an
 expert agency.  The Committee is of the view that the matter of revival and amalgamation of CIWTC should be got examined by some high powered expert committee.   The Committee once again reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in 117
th Report on Demands for Grants 2007-08 of Department of Shipping, which is reproduced below:
“The Committee is constrained to note that inspite of its recommendation in the past, the Government has not come out with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of River Service Division (RSD). The Committee is of the opinion that CIWTC with its infrastructure and expertise can play an integral part for development and
 promotion of inland water transport through NW-I and NW-II. The Committee recommends that possibility may also be explored to physically amalgamate the remaining CIWTC with Inland Water Transport Authority of India (IWAI) or Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), so that the infrastructure and expertise of

DEVELOPMENT OF WATER TRANSPORT IN ANDAMAN & NICOBAR AND LAKSHADWEEP ISLANDS
101.     The Shipping Corporation of India with its two owned passenger-cum-cargo vessels and 27 managed vessels operates domestic passenger-cum-transportation services between mainland and Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshdweep group of islands on behalf of the Government of India.  Presently, Andaman and Nicobar Island administration has 22
 vessels comprising of 18 passenger vessels and 4 passenger-cum-cargo vessels, Union Territory of Lakshdweep has 5 vessels comprising 1 passenger-cum-cargo vessel, 3 passenger vessels and one bunker barge.  The Committee observes that water transport is the life-line of these groups of islands for their interconnection with the mainland and within islands. 
 The Committee notes that this sector has been neglected for so many years without any fund infusion for modernization of the vessels and purchase of additional vessels.  Due to this, the populations of these islands are suffering to a great extent.  The Committee further notes that in the Demand-for-Grants for the year 2008-09 no financial allocation has been
 made for improving the interconnectivity and water transport in Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshdweep islands.  The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Government of India to take immediate steps for improving inter-islands connectivity of the islands of Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshdweep for mitigating the problems of connectivity
 between these islands.  The Committee also recommends that sufficient Budgetary Allocation may be provided for augmenting the water transport connectivity in these islands.

ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2008-09
The Committee observes that the Department has projected a requirement of Rs.68971.48 crore for the entire 11 th Plan.  Against this requirement, the Planning Commission approved an allocation of Rs.67173.40 crore to the Department for carrying out major activities i.e. development of Major Ports, Inland Water Transport,
 procurement of Dredgers and connected activities for the Dredging Corporation of India, Constructions of landing facility  in Andnman and Nicobar Islands, post Tsunami rehabilitation works, Ship Building, Rail Connectivity for the ports and Setusamundrum  Ship Channel Project etc. 
(Para 10)
            The Committee strongly deplores the tendency of Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for imposing cuts on the amount demanded by the Department as per their pressing needs.  The Committee feels that if the Department of Shipping has to attain the national growth of 9% in the 11 th Plan period, it will require huge
 and well planned funding.  Thus, the Government spending for the Department of Shipping will have to be significantly stepped up from the present level to meet the growth targets.  The Committee ,therefore, strongly recommends that the Department should be provided with Rs.68971.48 crore by the Planning Commission and the
 Ministry of Finance for the 11th Plan period as per their original proposal and ensure that no project/scheme proposed by the Department would languish for want of funds.  The Committee also recommends the Department to take appropriate caution and remedial action to absorb in time the allocation made to them.
(Para 11)
            The Committee is perturbed to note that the Department of Shipping has projected higher plan outlays of Rs.4271.27 crore during the year 2007-08 which was drastically reduced to Rs. 3075.34 crore at RE stage and ultimately, the Department failed to utilize the reduced amount too.  The Department utilized Rs. 2517.00 crore during
 2007-08 against the budget estimates of Rs.4271.27 crore and surrendered an amount of Rs.1754.27 crore as compared to the BE for the year. The Committee observes that the saving affects almost all the major activities of Department of Shipping be it Inland Water Transport, Shipping, Ports, Lighthouses and Lightships, Shipbuilding etc.
 and the actual expenditure incurred has always been abysmally low compared to the estimated amount. The Committee is not satisfied with the reasons furnished by the Department for non-utilization of the allocations for their being either vague or of routine in nature.  The Committee does not approve the practice being followed by the
 Department which has been asking for higher allocations year after year, but the implementation of projects and schemes were poor as ground realities were not taken into account while formulating and implementing the projects.  The Committee is pained to note that although they have repeatedly recommended for formulation of realistic
 plans and schemes but no action have been taken by the Government on those recommendations.  The Committee expects that intensified monitoring mechanism which is being put in place by the Department, would ensure that budgeted amounts earmarked at the BE stage are fully utilized during 2008-09. 1
REPORT
The Department of Road Transport and Highways under the Ministry of Shipping, Road
Transport and Highways has been entrusted primarily with the functions of construction and
maintenance of National Highways (NH), administration of Motor V ehicle Act and Central Motor
Vehicles Rules, formulation of broad policies relating to road transport, environmental issues,
relating to vehicular movements automotive norms, etc. besides making arrangements for
movements of vehicular traffic with neighbouring countries.
2. India has a vast road network of 3.32 million km. of which the National Highways and
the State Highways together account for 1,95,000 kms. The length of National Highways
network is only 66754 kms. (at present) constituting about 2 per cent of the total road network
in the country and carrying about 40 per cent of the total traffic across the length and breadth
of the country. The number of vehicles has been growing at a rapid pace of 12 per cent per
annum and consequently traffic on the roads is growing at 7-10 per cent per annum. The share
of roads in total traffic has been growing from 12 per cent of freight traffic and 31.6 per cent
of the passenger traffic in 1950-51 to a projected 65 per cent of freight traffic and 87 per cent
of passenger traffic.
3. To cope with this increase, appropriate expansion and improvement of the road network
is necessary. All this requires a massive infusion of funds. Historically, investments in roads,
especially highways, were mainly made by the Government because of the large volume of
resources required, long gestation period of projects, uncertain returns and various associated
externalities. But in recent times, the private sector has been actively involved in the development
and maintenance of the National Highways. The Ministry has formulated policy guidelines to
encourage private sector participation in the highway sector, besides providing several incentives
such as tax exemptions and duty free import of road building equipment and machinery. Model
Concession Agreements have also been finalized for major road projects.
4. The Road Transport Wing of the Department is concerned with the formulation of broad
policies related to road transport besides making provisions for the movement of vehicular traffic
with the neighbouring countries. The following Acts/Rules which embody the policy relating to
motor vehicles and State Transport Corporations are being administered in the Road Transport
Wing of the Department:—
• The Motor V ehicles Act, 1988
• The Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989
• The Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950
• The Carriers Act, 1865
5. The development and maintenance of National Highways are being done on agency basis.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), State Public Works Departments (PWDs) and
the Border Roads Organisation are the main agencies. Out of the total National Highways length
of 66754 km, about 19706 km. have been entrusted to National Highways Authority of India
(NHAI) for improvement under National Highway Development Project (NHDP), and some other
non NHDP scheme. About 46050 km. length of National Highways is at present entrusted to
State PWDs and Border Road Organisation (BRO) as agencies of the Ministry and about 998 km.
length are yet to be entrusted.

2
6. Our country having one of the largest road networks of 3.32 million km., consists of
expressways, National Highways, State Highways, Major District Roads, Other District Roads and
Village Roads with following length distribution:
National Highways/Expressways : 66754 km.
State Highways : 128000 km.
Major and other District Roads : 470000 km.
Rural Roads : 2650000 km.
7. The National Highways have further been classified depending upon the width formation.
Generally, a lane has a width of 3.75 metres in case of single lane and 3.5 metres in case of
multi lane National Highways. The break-up of National Highways in terms of width is as under:
Single Lane/Intermediate lane 18350 km. 27%

26. The Committee notes that the growth of Motor Vehicles in India is unprecedented.
The process of liberalization and globalization augmented the number of vehicles to
beyond the imagination of our planners of road sector development. The infrastructure
available is not at all commensurate with the growth of vehicles. The Committee also
notes that the allocation to the Department is almost static in real terms. There is an
increase of 20 per cent in Annual Plan outlay and 7.6 per cent in budgetary support. The
above increase in Annual Plan outlay and budgetary support may not be adequate even
to meet the increase in cost. Thus, it poses a great mismatch between the availability of
the road infrastructure and vehicular population.
27. Inadequate development of road sector will result in congested roads, traffic jams,
recurring accidents and chaos in the road sector. Moreover, the development of road
infrastructure is immensely important to sustain the growth of the economy. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should allot funds to the

recommends that demands of the Department may be acceded to at the RE stage.

30. The National Highways Development Project (NHDP) — the largest Highway Project ever
undertaken by the country, which is being implemented by the NHAI, consists of the following

30.2 NHDP Phase-II is the work of upgradation of 6644 km. mainly consisting of stretches

30.4 The Phase-IV involves upgradation of about 20000 kms. of National Highways to 2 lane

Government.

30.5 The Government has approved six laning of 6500 km. of existing 4-lane National

30.6 The NHDP Phase-VI consists of the work of construction of 1000 km. of Expressways
on Design-Build-Finance-Operate (DBFO) basis with an estimated cost of Rs.16,680 crore has
been approved by the Government in November, 2006.
NHDP PHASE-VII
30.7 The Government has approved construction of ring roads, bypasses, grade separators,
flyovers, elevated roads and tunnels at a cost of Rs.16,680 crore under the NHDP Phase-VII.
Of the total cost, Rs.6,302 crore will be provided by the government while Rs.l0,378 crore will
come from the private sector. The larger chunk of the total investments about Rs.10,500 crore
will be spent on construction of 700 km. of ring roads and bypasses. The remaining amount
of Rs.6,180 crore will be spent on stand alone grade separated intersections, road over
bridges, elevated roads, tunnels, underpasses and service roads. The works of stand alone ring
roads and bypasses are likely to be awarded by March, 2011 and is likely to be completed by
December, 2014.

9
31. The Committee notes that majority of the work of NHDP Phase-II which was
conceived in the year 2003 has yet to be completed. The Committee would like to know
the reasons for the delay and the agencies/officers responsible for it. The Committee
recommends that the Government may take immediate effective steps to complete the
project. The Committee also notes that the NHDP Phase-IV is yet to be approved by the
Government however, no reasons therefor have been given. It is pity that 20000 km., a
major part of local NH, is yet to brought to 2 lane standards under Phase-IV but the
project has not been approved till date by the Government. The Committee recommends
that NHDP Phase-IV may be considered by the Government for approval immediately. The
progress of the projects under other phases may be monitored regularly so as to ensure
their timely implementation.
FUNDING OF NHAI PROJECTS
32. To a specific query on the funding of such mega projects, the Department replied that
the NHAI depends on Government support for implementing most of its projects, whether it is
by way of Capital contribution towards cost or by way of Viability Gap Support. The
Government funds to NHAI are released on two accounts:—
(i) The petrol/HSD cess which is provided as investment, with the current year
provision being Rs.6972.47 crores;
(ii) As EAP assistance, under which for the current year, the grant is Rs.1515 crores
and loan component is Rs.379 crores.
33. Further to the above, the NHAI has also been raising funds from the market to fund
various activities. During the year 2008-09, the NHAI proposes to raise Rs.4100 crores  from the
market, the repayment of the borrowings will also be done through the cess funding.

34. The Committee was informed that the Government of India, enacted the Central Road

56. Road transport is considered to be one of the cost effective and preferred mode of

people in the country are resorting to excessive use of private vehicles and this has put
the roads under undue pressure. The Committee observes that most of the investment on
roads is being extracted from the public itself but the returns accruing to the users are
not equitable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the efforts of the Government
should focus on developing public transport, which discourages excessive use of private
vehicles. The Government should adopt a methodology, whereby, in the more densely
populated states, the rich and the affluent are asked to pay more for keeping more than
one vehicle.
CREATION OF NATIONAL ROAD SAFETY BOARD
90. The Committee was informed that the Committee on Road Safety and Traffic
Management constituted under the Chairmanship of Shri S. Sundar, Former  Secretary of erstwhile
M/o Surface Transport and Distinguished fellow, TERI has submitted its report to Hon’ble
Minister, S,RT and H on 20.2.2007. The Committee has recommended creation of a National
Road Safety Board under a separate Act of the Parliament. A note in this regard has been sent
to Cabinet Secretariat on 10.1.08. Since there is long way to go for constitution of this Board,
it has been proposed to allocate a token amount i.e. Rs.0.01 crore under this head for the year
2008-09.
91. When the Committee expressed its disappointment over the delay in the establishment of
National Road Safety and Traffic Board, the Secretary responded:
“.....What they have recommended is based on experience in other countries where road
safety is really given a very high priority. What they have said is really practical and
perhaps will be an effective way of handling the issue. Normally, what happens is these
Boards are set up, but there is no source of funding. They are suggesting one percent
Cess to be earmarked for road safety. For that they are suggesting amendment to the
Central Road Fund also. That is perhaps the right way. In there functions and duties all
this included”.
92. The Committee feels that the time has come for the creation of the much talked
about National Road Safety Board as the number of road accidents on national highways
is increasing in an alarming manner. The Committee recommends that the Department
should pursue the matter vigorously and take necessary actions to establish this Board at
the earliest.
TOLL TAX ON BRIDGES AND NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
93. The issue of collection of toll tax on bridges and national highways was raised by the
Committee during the course of evidence by the Secretary, Department of Road Transport and
Highways. The Committee in its 67th and 118th reports discussed the subject in detail and
recommended that once the cost of construction of a roadlbridge plus interest is recovered, the
collection of toll should be stopped. The Committee also felt that there exists a need for the
rationalisation of the toll tax being charged on the National Highways. To a specific

21
recommendation of the Committee in its 118th Report for creation of one time revolving fund,
the Department replied that present levy of cess is tied up for the implementation of NHDP and
Prime Minister’s Gram Sadak Yojana and the improvement of sanctioned works of State Road.
Therefore, it may not be possible to create a revolving fund until and unless the amount of cess
is increased. However, this is being taken up with Ministry of Finance.
94. The Committee once again recommends that once the capital and interest is
recovered, the users’ fee must be discontinued. The Committee is of the opinion that
there is a need for establishment of a regulator to determine the reasonable return to
the investor on road projects which is being considered as a yardstick for fixation of toll.
The Committee appreciates that in view of the resource crunch being faced by the
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and there is a genuine need for generation of
additional revenue by the Ministry. Whenever any National Highway is constructed, it
leads to huge value addition to the land adjoining the National Highway and these benefits
of addition in value have so far  been enjoyed by private agencies only. The Government
should also get advantage of the appreciation of land value because it is the taxpayer’s
money that has led to the value addition of that property. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Government may explore the possibility of imposing some cess/tax
on land adjoining National Highways which is being utilized for commercial purpose on
annual basis. This could serve as a permanent source of income for the Government and
the revenue so generated could be ploughed back for the construction and maintenance
of National Highways in the country. Provision of ducting at the time of construction of
National Highways for laying telephone and electric cables also leads to value addition and
can be explored for generating more funds for the road sector. These measures may go
a long way to meet the resource gap for maintenance and construction of National
Highways in the country.

22
OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
ANNUAL PLAN 2007-08
The Committee observed that out of the RE (2007-08) Plan allocation
of Rs.14066.00 crore, an amount of Rs.11887.44 was spent (provisional) up to
12th March, 2008 which stands at 84.5 per cent of RE. The overall expenditure profile of
the Department is also not showing any encouraging trends. Out of Rs.16481.85 crore
(RE) for the year 2007-08, a sum of Rs.13338.03 crore was expended (provisional) till the
12th March, 2008 which stands at 81.0 per cent of the RE. This is very much in contrast
to the quantum of expenditure incurred in the year 2006-07 where it stood at a good
97.9 per cent of RE allocated for that year. (Para 11)
The Committee finds that despite its earlier recommendations on the aspect of
funds utilization and the need for constant monitoring of projects, the Department of
Road Transport and Highways has done pr ecious little to improve the situation. This is
evident from the reply of the Department with regard to non-utilisation of funds that the
allocation for road sector is based on anticipated implementation of projects every year.
The Committee is of the opinion that the road sector plays a vital role in providing good
infrastructure in the country. The Committee feels that submission of routine replies for
under utilization of funds and poor performance in achieving the physical targets is not
going to yield any result. Instead of that the Department may list out the bottlenecks and
draw a strategy to overcome such bottlenecks. The Committee is of the opinion that
active involvement of project executing agencies such as PWD, NHAI and State
Governments would only help the Department in utilizing its fund to the maximum
extent. The Committee, therefore, recommends that proper co-ordination with all these
organizations should be maintained in order to achieve physical targets satisfactorily.
(Para 15)
ANNUAL PLAN 2008-09
The Committee notes that the growth of Motor Vehicles in India is unprecedented.
The process of liberalization and globalization augmented the numbet of vehicles to
beyond the imagination of our planners of road sector development. The infrastructure
available is not at all commensurate with the  growth of vehicles. The Committee also
notes that the allocation to the Department is almost static in real terms. There is an
increase of 20 per cent in Annual Plan outlay and 7.6 per cent in budgetary support. The
above increase in Annual Plan outlay and budgetary support may not be adequate even
to meet the increase in cost. Thus, it poses a great mismatch between the availability of
the road infrastructure and vehicular population, Inadequate development of road sector
will result in congested roads, traffic jams, recurring accidents and chaos in the road
sector. Moreover, the development of road infrastructure is immensely important to
sustain the growth of the economy. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Government should allot funds to the Department of Road Transport and Highways so as
to ensure the development of road infrastructure in proportion to the growth of vehicles.
The Committee further recommends that demands of the Department may be acceded to
at the RE stage. (Para 26 & 27)

23
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
The Committee notes that majority of the work of NHDP Phase-II which was
conceived in the year 2003 has yet to be completed. The Committee would like to know
the reasons for the delay and the agencies/officers responsible for it. The Committee
recommends that the Government may take immediate effective steps to complete the
project. The Committee also notes that the NHDP phase-IV is yet to be approved by the
Government however, no reasons therefor have been given. It is pity that 20000 km, a
major part of local NH, is yet to be brought to 2 lane standards under Phase-IV but the
project has not been approved till date by the Government. The Committee recommends
that NHDP Phase-IV may be considered by the Government for approval immediately. The
progress of the projects under other phases may be monitored regularly so as to ensure
their timely implementation. (Para 31)

The Committee notes that there is a gradual decrease in the allocation of
funds for improvement of State roads particularly during the year 2004-05 amount of
Rs.101.14 crore for projects under Economic Importance and Rs.232.94 crores for projects
under Inter-State Connectivity has gone down to Rs.27.53 crores and Rs.132.66 crores
respectively during 2007-08. The Committee hopes that the trend may be reversed and the
State Roads may get more and more allocation which may be properly utilized for the
improvement of various state roads connectivity.
The Committee is unhappy with the delay in finalizing the Detailed Project Report
on Mughal Road in Jammu and Kashmir as a result of which the competent authority
could not sanction the project. The Government, however, has not given any reason as to
why there was delay in finalizing the Detailed Project Report. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department to apprise the Committee about those reasons and
action taken in the matter. The Committee desires that the Department should fine tune
its systems and procedures to avoid such delays. (Para 40 & 41)
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS (ORIGINAL) WORKS: NH(O)
The Committee is not happy with the mere 15.90 per cent increase in allocation
for the maintenance of national highways. The Committee was informed that an amount
of Rs.2280 crores is required for maintenance and repair of roads annually. The
Committee is of the opinion that Government should give adequate importance for the
maintenance and repair of non-NHDP highways to ensure that investment made in the NH
does not go waste. The Committee recommends that one third of the cess collected for
the financing NHDP projects should be allocated for the maintenance and repair of
highways. The Committee desires that the Department should take up the issue with the
Planning Commission for getting one third portion of the cess collected for the
maintenance and repair of national highways as these non-NHDP national highways are
considered as lifeline of Indian transport sector. (Para 45)
DEVELOPMENT OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS IN NORTH-EASTERN REGION
The Committee notes that lot of programmes are on the anvil for the development
of National Highways in the North-East. The Committee hopes that the Department may
be able to utilize the entire allocated amount for the North-East. (Para 49)

24
CENTRAL ROAD FUND
The Committee notes that the petrol pumps which are collecting the cess, hardly
give any bills for the purchase of petroleum products. In this way, the Committee
apprehends that the exchequer may be loosing hundreds of crores of rupees as the exact
amount collected may always be under reported. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that it may be apprised about the mechanism and procedure available for collection of
cess towards Central Road Fund.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Railways which itself capable to
undertake developmental works, wherever required may do so from its own resources/
profits instead of seeking allocation from the Central Road Fund. (Para 54 & 55)
ROAD SAFETY
The Committee feels that school children are the best messiahs for preaching road
safety to their parents. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the road safety
campaign may give adequate importance to this aspect and the Department may rope in
schools and school children to spread awareness for road safety. The work done by the
NGOs for raising road safety awareness may also be given due publicity in media and
local newspapers. This may ensure the better functioning of NGOs and the public in
general will keep watch on their activities. (Para 64)
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
The Committee feels that this is a welcome step. The Committee recommends that
the number of organization sponsored by the Ministry is very low and insufficient
compared to the vastness of our transport sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Government may endeavor to finance at least one NGO in each of the districts
of the country for imparting refresher course to the drivers of Heavy Motor Vehicles. The
Committee also recommends that a proper monitoring mechanism may be put in place to
'ensure that the organizations are actually imparting training to the drivers.
The Committee notes that the Planning Commission has discontinued the scheme
of Model Driving Training Schools. The Committee may be apprised the reasons for the
discontinunance of the scheme. The Committee would also like to know whether any
alternative schemes are proposed by the Planning Commission to fill the gap of Model
Driving Training Schools.
The States where Model Driving Training Schools were sanctioned may be asked to
complete the projects in a time bound manner and funds may be allotted accordingly.

trauma care. At the very same time the Committee feels that the present allocation of

Strengthening public transport system including introduction of IT like

Report
The tourism has been a major social phenomenon of the societies all along.  It is motivated by the natural urge of every
 human being for new experience, adventure, education and entertainment.  Tourism is a multi sectoral activity characterized by
 multiple services provided by a range of suppliers.  It is largest service industry in the country.  Its importance lies in being an
 instrument for economic development and employment generation.   The tourism has been pivotal in social progress as well as
 an important vehicle of widening socio-economic and cultural contacts throughout human history.  A wide array of interests-
entertainment, sports, religion, culture,  adventure, education, health and business- drives tourism through increased contact.   It
 helps to promote cultural cohesion and social bonding and creates a durable social fabric.  With the advancement of transport,
 communication and improvement in general economic well being the demand for tourism has increased manifold.   The Five-
Year Plan perspective initiatives required for the development of tourism synergize with the development efforts needed to
 accomplish a number of other goals like employment generation, advancement of women and disadvantaged groups.  The
 Government plays a crucial role in making provision for tourism infrastructure and skill development. Such initiatives
 catalyses private enterprises to come forward and invest in this sector.  The share of India in international tourist arrival
 continues to increase from 2004 onwards.  But the share is still low at 0.55% in 2007.  The foreign tourist arrival rose from
 3.46 million in 2004 to an estimated 5 million in 2007.  Further more, foreign exchange earnings from tourism in India rose
 substantially from US$3 billion in 2002 to an estimated US$ 11.96 billion in 2007.  The share of India in world’s tourism
 receipts scaled from 0.65 per cent in 2002 to 1.21 percent in 2006. 
2.         The Ministry of Tourism is the nodal agency for the formulation of national policies and programmes and for the
 coordination of activities of various Central Government agencies, State Governments/Union Territories and the Private Sector
 for the development and promotion of tourism in the country.  The Ministry of Tourism plays a crucial role in coordinating and
 supplementing the efforts of the State/Union Territories Governments, catalyzing private investment, strengthening
 promotional and marketing efforts and in providing trained manpower resources. The function of the Ministry of Tourism
 mainly consists of the following:-
·
        Framing of policy matters on development of tourism
·        Grant of Central Financial Assistance to States/UTs for Development of Tourism Infrastructure
·        Encouragement of Public Private participation in tourism infrastructure development
·        Promotion and marketing of Tourism Products within the country and abroad
·        Providing incentives in the accommodation sector
·        Regulation of tourism industry
·        Investment facilitation
·        Human Resource Development and Training
·        Research, analysis, monitoring and evaluation
·        International Cooperation of promotion and development of India Tourism
3.         The administrative head of the Ministry is the Secretary (Tourism).  The Secretary also acts as the Director General
 (DG) Tourism. The office of the Director General of Tourism {now merged with the office of Secretary (Tourism)} provides
 executive directions for the implementation of various policies and programmes.  Directorate General of Tourism has a field
 formation of 20 offices within the country and 13 offices abroad and one sub-ordinate office/project i.e. Indian Institute  of
 Skiing and Mountaineering (IISM)/Gulmarg Winter Sports Project (GWSP). The activities of IISM/GWSP have been revived

22.       The Committee notes that one of the reasons for underutilization of allocation is unspent balances with the States and
 also non-submission of utilization certificates by most of the States on time.  The Committee observes that most of the time the
 Central Government delay release of funds to the State or releases it at the fag end of the financial year and expects the States
 to utilize it in a very short time.  The Committee criticize this practice as obviously the States are not in a position to spend the
 entire amount in such a short period and therefore, have unspent balance lying with them.   The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the release of the funds to the States should be made on time so that they could utilize the amount rationally
 under proper monitoring of expenditure.   The Committee also desires that there should be proper coordination with the States
 Government, so as to obtain utilization certificates and to safeguard that money released is spent only on approved
 infrastructure development projects.
23.       The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is making efforts to develop quality tourism infrastructure at major
 tourist destinations and circuits for developing tourist products and providing better services to both domestic and international
 tourists.  The Committee observes that tourism is one of the economic sectors in the country that has the potential to grow at
 high rate and can ensure consequential development of the infrastructure of the destinations and circuits.  The Committee feels
 that the infrastructure development holds the key to India’s sustained of growth in the tourism sector,  therefore, tourist sites
 and destinations needs to be carefully selected on the basis of their potential to provide all infrastructural  facilities  required by
 the tourists within such destinations and circuits.   The Committee is of the opinion that, if, India has to exploit its vast inherent
 potential  in tourism, then it must provide exclusive quality tourism product and destinations comparable with other Asian
 countries like Singapore, Malaysia, Maldives, Thailand and China. As tourism cannot develop independent of other
 infrastructure, therefore, a lot of information dissemination is required in addition to hospitality and the scope and reach of the
 domestic tourism should also be broadened through development of these competitive destinations and circuits.   The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to develop quality tourism at identified tourist circuits and destinations with
 focus on mega destinations and circuits that match international standards and satisfy the domestic and international tourists.  
 The aggressive marketing and publicity of these destinations and circuits should also be done to generate a niche market for
 Indian tourism products.   The Committee also urges the Ministry that while selecting a destination or a circuit they should
 attach priority for harmonious growth and development of all the Regions and States. 
24.       The Committee also recommends that in order to maximize the impact of investment on tourism infrastructure, the
 Ministry should make efforts for convergence of these mega destinations and circuits and projects with Jawahar Lal Nehru
 National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) for integrated development of infrastructure services, urban renewal, asset
 management and urban governance.

 Parliament from the North – Eastern States have also raised this issue in the Consultative Committee and the Standing

MULTIPLICITY OF TAXES
84.       The Committee in its various Reports on Demands for Grants of Ministry of Tourism has dealt with the matter of
 Multiplicity of Taxes and recommended the Government for ensuring uniformity and rationalization of multiple taxes which
 has adverse impact on the tourism sector.  The Ministry of Tourism in their Action Taken Notes informed the Committee that
 the issue had been followed up with the Member Secretary, Empowered Committee of Finance Ministers, that the proposal of
 Ministry of Tourism regarding rationalization of taxes on tourism sector be taken up during the meeting of Empowered
 Committee.  In addition, this matter would again be taken up with respective State Government.   The Ministry of Tourism is
 aware that multiplicity of taxes in the tourism sector as well as the variation of quantum of taxes levied by different States and
 Union Territories does affect the growth of tourism in the country. Some of the major taxes which are having an adverse affect
 in growth of tourism are the luxury tax on hotel, VAT on food and beverages and on Airlines Turbine Fuel (ATF).  In addition,
 there is huge variation on taxes on tourist transport vehicles in the States.The Ministry of Tourism has forwarded a detailed
 proposal on the rationalization of the above taxes to the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance and has also taken up this
 issue with the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers.
85.       In order to rationalize the tax on tourist transport and to facilitate smooth movement of inter-state travel, the Ministry of
 Tourism has mooted a proposal regarding introduction of Zonal Permits for a minimum of 3 States.  It has been suggested that
 the States may agree to the Tourist Transport by Operators depositing a composite tax per State, per quarter, per bus.  The tax
 component to a particular State could then be deposited in separate designated bank accounts of each State so as to ensure
 there is no loss of revenue to each of the State in the zone.  The second suggestion which has been mooted to complement the
 above recommendation is introduction of a separate Tourists Vehicles (T.V.) series as registration number for Government of
 India approved Tourist Transport Operators.  This will enable easy identification of tourist transport vehicles at border crossing
 and distinguish them from State carriages. The first proposal was forwarded to the Department of Revenue to be taken up with
 the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers.  The second proposal has been taken up with the Ministry of Road
 Transport and State Governments.  A decision in this regard is awaited from the respective quarters.
86.       The Committee is constrained to notes that luxury tax on hotel, VAT on food and beverages and on Aviation Turbine
 Fuel (ATF) and higher rate of taxes on tourist transport vehicles in the States have adverse effect on the growth of tourism.  
 The Committee, however, is perturbed to note that even after repeated recommendations of the Committee,  the Government
 has not been able to do much to rationalize the tax regime, which is ailing the tourism sector at large.  The Ministry of Tourism
 has forwarded two proposals for consideration of Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers and Department of Road
 Transport and Highways respectively, in this regard and a decision is awaited.   The Committee strongly criticizes the
 lackadaisical approach of the Government in the matter which has adversely affected the growth of tourism and hospitality
 sector in the country.   The Committee reiterates that the Government must provide a level playing field to the tourism and
 hospitality sector including tourist transport by attempting to rationalize taxes or eliminate the disparity in tax treatment as
 levied by the different States and Union Territories.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to pursue vigorously the matter
 of rationalization of taxes with the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers till the matter is favourably resolved. 
 The Committee also recommends the Government to set up an Empowered Group for rationalization of roads and transport
 taxes on tourist vehicles.
